text: EX-10.4 2 ea031087801ex10-4.htm FORBEARANCE AGREEMENT AND AMENDMENT TO DEBENTURES, DATED AS OF OCTOBER 29, 2026, AMONG THE COMPANY, THE GUARANTORS (AS DEFINED THEREIN), JGB PARTNERS, LP, JGB CAPITAL, LP, JGB CAPITAL OFFSHORE LTD., JGB ORPINGTON, LLC AND CHICAGO ATLANTIC ADAMS, LLC Exhibit 10.4 FORBEARANCE AGREEMENT AND AMENDMENT TO DEBENTURES This FORBEARANCE AGREEMENT AND AMENDMENT TO DEBENTURES (this “Agreement”) is entered into as of October 29, 2026 (the “Signing Date”), by and among LIVEONE, INC., a Delaware corporation (the “Company”), each of the undersigned Subsidiaries of the Company party to the Subsidiary Guarantee (each, a “Guarantor” and, together with the Company, the “Loan Parties” and each a “Loan Party”), JGB PARTNERS, LP, JGB CAPITAL, LP, JGB CAPITAL OFFSHORE LTD., JGB ORPINGTON, LLC and CHICAGO ATLANTIC ADAMS, LLC (collectively, the “Holders” and each a “Holder”), and JGB COLLATERAL LLC, as collateral agent for the Holders (in such capacity, the “Agent” and, together with the Holders, the “Lender Parties”). RECITALS (A) The Company and the Holders are parties to the Securities Purchase Agreement, dated as of May 19, 2025 (as amended, including by the Consent dated as of August 5, 2025, the “Purchase Agreement”), pursuant to which the Company issued to the Holders its 11.75% Original Issue Discount Senior Secured Convertible Debentures due May 19, 2028, each with an Original Issue Date of May 19, 2025 (each, a “Debenture” and collectively, the “Debentures”). (B) The obligations of the Company under the Debentures and the other Transaction Documents are guaranteed by the Guarantors pursuant to the Subsidiary Guarantee, dated as of May 19, 2025 (the “Subsidiary Guarantee”), and secured by the Collateral pursuant to the Security Agreement, dated as of May 19, 2025 (the “Security Agreement”), by and among the Company, the Guarantors, the Holders and the Agent, the Account Control Agreements and the other Security Documents, including the Uncertificated Securities Control Agreement among the Company, the Agent and VStock Transfer, LLC (“VStock”), as transfer agent for PodcastOne, Inc. (“PODC”) (the “PODC Control Agreement”). (C) Section 6(b) of each Debenture requires the Company, at all times while the Debentures remain outstanding, to maintain on deposit in one account of a US incorporated bank, subject to an Account Control Agreement, unencumbered cash in an amount equal to the lesser of (x) $7,500,000 and (y) the aggregate outstanding principal amount of all Debentures multiplied by 1.5 (the “Cash Minimum”). (D) The Loan Parties have requested that the Lender Parties forbear from exercising their rights and remedies that may be available to the Lender Parties under the Security Agreement and the other Transaction Documents (as defined in the Purchase Agreement) as of the date of this Agreement, and agree to certain amendments of the Debentures, and the Lender Parties are willing to do so solely on the terms and subject to the conditions set forth in this Agreement. NOW, THEREFORE, in consideration of the foregoing and the mutual covenants herein contained, and for other good and valuable consideration, the receipt and sufficiency of which are hereby acknowledged, the parties hereto agree as follows: Page 1 Section 1. Definitions 1.1 Capitalized terms used but not defined herein have the meanings given to them in the Debentures or, if not defined therein, the Purchase Agreement. As used herein: (i) “Cash Target” means $7,500,000. (ii) “Forbearance Period” means the period beginning on the Effective Date and ending on the earliest of (i) the date on which a Forbearance Termination Event occurs and (ii) payment in full of the Obligations. (iii) “Obligations” means all principal, interest, Prepayment Premium, Prepayment Amounts, liquidated damages, fees (including the Exit Fee and the Forbearance Fee), costs, expenses and other amounts owing by any Loan Party under the Debentures, this Agreement and the other Transaction Documents. (iv) “Releasees” means each Lender Party and each of its predecessors, successors, assigns, parents, subsidiaries, affiliates, funds and managed accounts, and each of their respective officers, directors, managers, members, partners, employees, attorneys, advisors and agents. Section 2. Acknowledgments of the Loan Parties 2.1 Obligations. Each Loan Party acknowledges, reaffirms and ratifies that, as of October 22, 2026, the aggregate Obligations in respect of the Debentures were not less than $15,130,182.95 (prior to the application of the Transferred Funds), consisting of outstanding principal, the applicable Prepayment Premium, accrued and unpaid interest, liquidated damages and other amounts, plus interest continuing to accrue thereon and fees, costs and expenses (including attorneys’ fees) chargeable under the Transaction Documents, all of which are justly owed without setoff, defense or counterclaim. Transferred Funds means an aggregate of $5,246,811.22 that was transferred from certain deposit accounts of the Loan Parties to the Agent prior to the Signing Date per the Agent’s transfer instructions (the “Transfer Instructions”) and credited towards repayment of the then outstanding Obligations. 2.2 Transferred Funds. Each Loan Party acknowledges that the Transfer Instructions were delivered, and the Transferred Funds were transferred, in accordance with the Account Control Agreements and the Security Agreement, and that the Agent is entitled to retain the Transferred Funds pursuant to Section 4.4. Section 3. Ratification; Waiver of Defenses 3.1 Ratification. Each Loan Party ratifies, reaffirms and confirms each Transaction Document to which it is a party and agrees that each such Transaction Document, as modified hereby, is and remains in full force and effect and is the legal, valid and binding obligation of such Loan Party, enforceable in accordance with its terms. Page 2 3.2 Liens. Each Loan Party ratifies and reaffirms each Lien granted by it to the Agent under the Security Documents and acknowledges that such Liens are valid, enforceable, perfected first-priority Liens on the Collateral (subject only to Permitted Liens) securing all of the Obligations, including the Obligations arising under this Agreement. 3.3 Guarantee. Each Guarantor acknowledges this Agreement and agrees that its obligations under the Subsidiary Guarantee are not released, diminished, impaired or otherwise adversely affected hereby and continue to guarantee the full payment and performance of all Obligations. 3.4 No Defenses. Each Loan Party represents, warrants and agrees that it has no defenses, counterclaims, offsets, rights of recoupment or other claims of any kind or nature against any Releasee with respect to the Obligations, the Transaction Documents, the Transfer Instructions and, to the extent any such defense, counterclaim, offset, recoupment or claim exists, it is hereby irrevocably and unconditionally waived. Section 4. Forbearance 4.1 Forbearance. Subject to the satisfaction of the conditions in Section 7 and the terms of this Agreement, during the Forbearance Period the Lender Parties shall forbear from exercising their rights and remedies under the Transaction Documents and applicable law solely in respect of any Event of Default that may have occurred and/or continued under Section 7(a)(iii) of each Debenture prior to the Signing Date. This forbearance is limited to such Events of Defaults and does not apply to any other Event of Default, whether now existing or hereafter arising. 4.2 Lender Parties Further Actions. Effective as of the Effective Date, the Holders shall provide such written instructions or communications (email shall suffice) to the Company, on behalf of the Loan Parties, as the Company shall reasonably request to evidence the agreements under this Agreement, provided that such instructions shall not affect any subsequent Event of Default or impair any right consequent thereon. 4.3 Account Instructions. Within one (1) Business Day after the Effective Date, the Agent shall deliver to such banks with which any Guarantor maintains a bank account a written notice, substantially in the form of Exhibit A. The Account Control Agreements shall remain in full force and effect, and the Agent may deliver such notice or instructions at any time as it deems available under the Transaction Documents after the occurrence of a Forbearance Termination Event. 4.4 Retention of Transferred Funds. Notwithstanding Section 4.3, the Agent shall retain all Transferred Funds. The Transferred Funds, together with the Top-Up Payment described in Section 5.3, shall be applied to the Obligations in such order as the Agent determines, including to the reimbursement of the Agent’s expenses in connection with the administration of the Obligations. Page 3 4.5 VStock Instruction. Within one (1) Business Day after the Effective Date, the Agent shall deliver to VStock a written notice, substantially in the form of Exhibit B. The PODC Control Agreement and the Agent’s Lien on any shares of PODC common stock pledged by the Company pursuant to the Transaction Documents (the “Pledged PODC Shares”) shall remain in full force and effect, and the Agent may issue such instructions to VStock at any time as Agent deems available under the Transaction Documents after the occurrence of a Forbearance Termination Event. 4.6 Default Interest. During the Forbearance Period, interest on the Debentures shall continue to accrue at the non-default Applicable Interest Rate (11.75% per annum) and be payable in cash monthly in accordance with Section 2(a) of the Debentures. Section 5. Forbearance Consideration; Required Payments 5.1 Forbearance Fee Shares. As a fee for the Lender Parties’ agreements herein, which fee is fully earned on the Signing Date and non-refundable, the Company shall on the Effective Date cause PODC to issue to the Holders (pro rata in accordance with their Pro Rata Shares, or as the Agent otherwise directs) an aggregate of 275,000 shares of PODC Common Stock (the “Fee Shares” and such fee, the “Forbearance Fee”), The Holders agree to the imprinting, so long as is required by applicable laws or regulations of the Commission, of a standard and customary Securities Act (as defined below) legend on any of the Fee Shares. In addition, the Company shall cause PODC to file with the Commission within thirty (30) days of the Effective Date (the “Filing Deadline”) and have declared effective within sixty (60) days of the Effective Date (or ninety (90) days in the event that the Registration Statement is subject to a review by the Commission) (the “Effectiveness Deadline”) a resale registration statement under the Securities Act of 1933, as amended (the “Securities Act”), in customary form, covering the resale of such Fee Shares by applicable Holder on a delayed or continuous basis under Rule 415 promulgated under the Securities Act and naming the applicable Holder as a selling security holder thereunder (the “Registration Statement”), and the Registration Statement is reasonably acceptable to the Agent; provided that the Agent shall promptly respond to any such PODC request to review the Registration Statement; provided, however, that if any such deadline falls on a Saturday, Sunday or any other day that the Commission is closed for business, such deadline shall be extended to the next Business Day on which the Commission is open for business. In connection with the preparation of the Registration Statement, each Holder shall provide to the Company and/or PODC such information as the Company and/or PODC shall reasonably request. If the Registration Statement is not filed with the Commission on or prior to the Filing Deadline or the Registration Statement is not declared effective by the Commission on or before the Effectiveness Deadline (other than as a result of the Commission not operating in the ordinary course of business for any reason), the Company will make a one-time payment to the Holders, as liquidated damages and not as a penalty (pro rata in accordance with their Pro Rata Shares, or as the Agent otherwise directs), in an aggregate amount equal to two percent (2%) of the aggregate then outstanding principal amount of the Debentures for each 30-day period (or pro rated portion thereof) that such Registration Statement is not so filed or declared effective, as applicable, subject to a maximum of four percent (4%). Such payments shall be made to the Holders in cash no later than fifteen (15) Business Days after the Filing Deadline, the Effectiveness Deadline or 30-day anniversary thereof, as applicable. Page 4 At the time any Holder was offered the Fee Shares, it was, and as of the date hereof it is, an “accredited investor” as defined in Rule 501(a)(1), (a)(2), (a)(3), (a)(7) or (a)(8) under the Securities Act. Each Holder understands that the Fee Shares are “restricted securities” and have not been registered under the Securities Act or any applicable state securities law and represents and warrants that it is acquiring the Fee Shares as principal for its own account and not with a view to or for distributing or reselling such Fee Shares or any part thereof in violation of the Securities Act or any applicable state securities law; provided, this representation and warranty shall not be deemed to limit such Holder’s right to sell the Fee Shares in compliance with applicable federal and state securities laws. Each Holder is not purchasing the Fee Shares as a result of any advertisement, article, notice or other communication regarding the Fee Shares published in any newspaper, magazine or similar media or broadcast over television or radio or presented at any seminar or any other general solicitation or general advertisement. 5.2 Initial Payment. On or before the date that is thirty (30) days after the Signing Date (i.e., November 30, 2026), the Company shall pay to the Agent, for the account of the Holders, $1,000,000 in cash by wire transfer of immediately available funds (the “Initial Payment”), which shall be applied to the Obligations in such order as the Agent determines; provided, however, that if any such deadline falls on a Saturday, Sunday or any other day that is not a Business Day, such deadline shall be extended to the next Business Day. 5.3 Cash Additional Payment. On or before the date that is sixty (60) days after the Signing Date (i.e., December 29, 2027), the Company shall pay to the Agent, for the account of the Holders, $1,250,000 in cash by wire transfer of immediately available funds (the “Additional Payment”); provided, however, that if any such deadline falls on a Saturday, Sunday or any other day that is not a Business Day, such deadline shall be extended to the next Business Day. The Additional Payment shall be applied to the Obligations in such order as the Agent determines. 5.4 Payments Generally. All payments hereunder shall be made without setoff, deduction or counterclaim, and are in addition to (and not in lieu of) scheduled interest and other payments under the Debentures, except as expressly modified by Section 6. Section 6. Amendments to Debentures Effective as of the Effective Date, and pursuant to Section 8(e) of each Debenture, each Debenture is amended as follows: 6.1 Cash Minimum. Effective upon the Agent’s receipt of the Initial Payment and/or Additional Payment plus amount of the Transferred Funds in an aggregate amount not less than the Cash Target (the “Cash Collateral Satisfaction Date”), (i) Section 6(b) of each Debenture is deleted in its entirety and replaced with “b) [Reserved]” and (ii) “Cash Minimum” shall mean $0 for purposes of Section 6(c) of each Debenture. 6.2 Monthly Redemption Schedule. Notwithstanding Section 4(a) of each Debenture: (i) the Holder Redemption Right for the calendar month of October 2026 is waived, and the portion of the Monthly Allowance for October 2026 that has not been redeemed shall remain outstanding as principal and be payable on the Maturity Date (or earlier in accordance with the Debentures); Page 5 (ii) the Holder Redemption Amount for the calendar month of November 2026 (equal to the Monthly Allowance for such month) shall be deferred and shall be due and payable on December 15, 2026, without further notice from any Holder; and (iii) commencing with the calendar month of December 2026, the Holder Redemption Right shall resume in accordance with Section 4(a) of each Debenture, with the Holder Redemption Amount for each calendar month due and payable no later than the last Trading Day of such month (i.e., December 31, 2026, January 29, 2027 and so on). 6.3 Exit Fee. A new Section 2(h) is added to each Debenture as follows: “h) Exit Fee. Upon the earlier of the Maturity Date or the consummation of any PODC Sale (whether before or after the payment in full of the Debentures), the Company shall pay to the Holders (based on their Pro Rata Shares as of the Signing Date), in cash, a fee (the “Exit Fee”) equal to the greater of (x) $1,000,000 and (y) 1.5% of the amount, if any, by which the PODC Sale Proceeds exceed $50,000,000. “PODC Sale” means (a) any sale, transfer or other Disposition, directly or indirectly, of all or any portion of the Equity Interests of PODC held by the Company or any Subsidiary in connection with a Change of Control Transaction of PODC, (b) any merger, consolidation or other transaction resulting in a Change of Control Transaction or Specified Carve-Out with respect to PODC, or (c) any Disposition of all or a material portion of the assets of PODC. “PODC Sale Proceeds” means the aggregate gross consideration (including cash, securities, assumed indebtedness and deferred or contingent consideration, valued at fair market value) received or receivable by the Company, PODC and their Subsidiaries, without duplication, in connection with a PODC Sale (excluding any financing or other non-sale consideration). If no PODC Sale has been consummated by the Maturity Date, then the Company shall pay $1,000,000 to the Holders (based on their Pro Rata Shares as of the Signing Date).” 6.4 Mandatory Prepayment Timing. The first two sentences of Section 2(f)(iv) of each Debenture are deleted in their entirety and replaced with the following: “iv. The Company shall deliver to the Holder written notice of any Mandatory Prepayment (such written notice, a “Mandatory Prepayment Notice”) promptly, and in any event not later than the date on which the Company or any Subsidiary publicly announces that it has entered into a definitive agreement for, or publicly announces, the transaction requiring such Mandatory Prepayment, and the date of consummation of such transaction shall be the “Mandatory Prepayment Date”. The amount payable for such Mandatory Prepayment set forth above (the “Mandatory Prepayment Amount”) shall be due and payable in full in cash prior to, or simultaneously with, the consummation of the Permitted Disposition, Change of Control Transaction or Specified Carve-Out Transaction requiring such Mandatory Prepayment, and no such transaction shall be consummated unless the Mandatory Prepayment Amount is paid in full concurrently therewith.” For the avoidance of doubt, the 40 Trading Day prior notice period formerly set forth in Section 2(f)(iv) is eliminated, and the remaining provisions of Section 2(f)(iv) (including the Holder’s conversion rights through payment in full, the Form 8-K requirement and default interest on unpaid amounts) shall continue to apply with references to the Mandatory Prepayment Date construed accordingly. 6.5 No Other Amendments. Except as expressly set forth in this Section 6, the Debentures and the other Transaction Documents remain unmodified and in full force and effect. Section 7. Conditions to Effectiveness 7.1 This Agreement (other than Sections 2, 3, 9 and 11, which are effective on the Signing Date) shall become effective on the date (the “Effective Date”) on which (x) the Agent and the Company shall have received counterparts of this Agreement duly executed by each Holder and (y) each of the following conditions has been satisfied or waived by the Agent: (i) the Agent shall have received counterparts of this Agreement duly executed by each Loan Party; and (ii) the Company shall have caused PODC to deliver to Vstock duly executed irrevocable instructions of PODC to issue the Fee Shares in accordance with Section 5.1, which shall be provided no later than October 30, 2026; Page 6 Section 8. Forbearance Termination Events; Remedies 8.1 Each of the following is a “Forbearance Termination Event”: (a) failure to pay the Initial Payment or the Additional Payment when due; (b) failure to pay any interest, Holder Redemption Amount (including the deferred November 2026 amount due December 15, 2026) or other amount when due under the Debentures, as modified hereby; (c) failure to deliver the Fee Shares as required by Section 5.1; (d) the occurrence of any Event of Default other than an Event of Default of which Agent may have notified the Company prior to the Signing Date; (e) any representation or warranty herein proving to have been untrue in any material respect when made; (f) any breach of any covenant herein which breach is not cured, if possible to cure, within 5 Trading Days after notice of such breach sent by the Agent to the Company; (g) any Loan Party or any Affiliate thereof commencing or joining any action challenging the validity or enforceability of this Agreement, any Transaction Document or any Lien of the Agent, or asserting any claim released hereunder; or (h) the occurrence of a Bankruptcy Event with respect to any Loan Party. 8.2 Upon the occurrence of a Forbearance Termination Event, automatically and without notice or any other action by any Lender Party: (a) the Forbearance Period shall terminate; (b) all Obligations shall be immediately due and payable; and (c) the Lender Parties may exercise any and all rights and remedies under the Transaction Documents and applicable law, including delivering any notices of exclusive control and transfer instructions under the Account Control Agreements, issuing any applicable instructions to VStock as Agent deems available under the Transaction Documents and applying the cash Collateral. The Loan Parties waive any notice, grace period or cure period with respect to the foregoing. Section 9. Release; Covenant Not to Sue 9.1 Release. In consideration of the Lender Parties’ agreements herein, each Loan Party, on behalf of itself and its predecessors, successors, assigns, parents, subsidiaries, affiliates, officers, directors, employees, agents and attorneys (collectively, the “Releasors”), hereby forever, fully, unconditionally and irrevocably releases and discharges each Releasee from any and all claims, demands, liabilities, obligations, debts, damages, causes of action (whether at law, in equity or otherwise), defenses, counterclaims and setoffs of any kind, whether known or unknown, suspected or unsuspected, liquidated or unliquidated, matured or unmatured, fixed or contingent, that any Releasor has or may have against any Releasee arising out of, connected with or related to any act, omission, event or circumstance existing or occurring on or prior to the Signing Date, including with respect to the Transaction Documents, the Obligations, the Transferred Funds, any enforcement or attempted enforcement of the Transaction Documents and the negotiation of this Agreement (collectively, the “Released Claims”). 9.2 Unknown Claims. Each Loan Party expressly waives the benefit of Section 1542 of the California Civil Code (and any similar law of any jurisdiction), which provides: “A GENERAL RELEASE DOES NOT EXTEND TO CLAIMS THAT THE CREDITOR OR RELEASING PARTY DOES NOT KNOW OR SUSPECT TO EXIST IN HIS OR HER FAVOR AT THE TIME OF EXECUTING THE RELEASE AND THAT, IF KNOWN BY HIM OR HER, WOULD HAVE MATERIALLY AFFECTED HIS OR HER SETTLEMENT WITH THE DEBTOR OR RELEASED PARTY.” 9.3 Covenant Not to Sue. Each Loan Party agrees that it shall not, and shall cause each other Releasor not to, commence, institute or prosecute any action or proceeding against any Releasee with respect to any Released Claim. This Section 9 shall survive the termination of this Agreement and the payment in full of the Obligations. Page 7 Section 10. Representations and Warranties 10.1 Each Loan Party represents and warrants to the Lender Parties that: (a) it has full power and authority to execute, deliver and perform this Agreement, which has been duly authorized by all necessary corporate or limited liability company action; (b) this Agreement constitutes its legal, valid and binding obligation, enforceable in accordance with its terms, except: (i) as limited by general equitable principles and applicable bankruptcy, insolvency, reorganization, moratorium and other laws of general application affecting enforcement of creditors’ rights generally, (ii) as limited by laws relating to the availability of specific performance, injunctive relief or other equitable remedies, and (iii) insofar as indemnification and contribution provisions may be limited by applicable law; (c) its execution, delivery and performance of this Agreement do not conflict with its organizational documents, any law or any material agreement binding on it, and require no consent of any Person not obtained, other than: (i) the notice and/or application(s) to the Principal Market for the issuance of the Fee Shares, (ii) the filing of Form D with the Commission, or (iii) the filings contemplated by Section 11 of this Agreement; (d) other than as contemplated by this Agreement, no Event of Default has occurred and is continuing; and (e) it is entering into this Agreement freely and voluntarily, with the advice of counsel of its choosing. Section 11. Disclosure 11.1 The Company shall disclose the material terms of this Agreement by not later than 5:30 p.m. (New York City time) on the fourth Trading Day following the Signing Date by means of a Current Report on Form 8-K filed with the Commission, which shall include this Agreement as an exhibit, and shall cause PODC to make any disclosure required of it. The Company and the Agent shall consult in preparing such report, and the Agent shall promptly respond to any Company request for comments on such report. From and after such filing, the Company acknowledges that no Lender Party shall be in possession of any material, non-public information received from the Company, PODC or any of their respective Subsidiaries, officers, directors, employees or agents. Section 12. Miscellaneous 12.1 Reservation of Rights. Except as expressly set forth herein, nothing herein constitutes a waiver of any Event of Default or any right or remedy of the Lender Parties, all of which are expressly reserved. No course of dealing shall arise from this Agreement, and the Lender Parties have no obligation to extend the Forbearance Period or to enter into any further forbearance or amendment. 12.2 Transaction Document. This Agreement is a Transaction Document and an amendment of the Debentures executed in accordance with Section 8(e) thereof. 12.3 Governing Law; Jurisdiction; Jury Waiver. The terms of Section 5.8 (Governing Law) of the Purchase Agreement are incorporated herein by reference, mutatis mutandis. IN ANY ACTION, SUIT OR PROCEEDING IN ANY JURISDICTION BROUGHT BY ANY PARTY AGAINST ANY OTHER PARTY, THE PARTIES EACH KNOWINGLY AND INTENTIONALLY, TO THE GREATEST EXTENT PERMITTED BY APPLICABLE LAW, HEREBY ABSOLUTELY, UNCONDITIONALLY, IRREVOCABLY AND EXPRESSLY WAIVE FOREVER TRIAL BY JURY. 12.4 Amendment; Entire Agreement; Severability. This Agreement may be amended only by a written agreement executed by the Company and the Holders of at least 50.1% of the outstanding principal amount of the Debentures (and, with respect to the rights or duties of the Agent, the Agent). This Agreement, together with the other Transaction Documents, constitutes the entire agreement of the parties with respect to its subject matter. If any provision hereof is held invalid, the remainder shall remain in full force and effect. 12.5 Counterparts. This Agreement may be executed in counterparts (including by electronic transmission or DocuSign or similar electronic signature service), each of which shall be an original and all of which together constitute one instrument. text: EX-10.1 2 ef20084865_ex10-1.htm EXHIBIT 10.1 Exhibit 10.1 November 3, 2026 Gregory J. Flesher Email: gflesh@gmail.com Re: Offer of Employment Dear Greg: Processa Pharmaceuticals, Inc. (the “ Company ”) is pleased to offer you at-will employment in the position of Chief Operating Officer (“ COO ”) on the terms and conditions set forth in this agreement (the “Agreement”). 1. Employment by the Company. Your employment with the Company shall begin on November 2, 2026 (the “ Start Date ”). This is an exempt position, and during your employment with the Company, you will devote your best efforts and substantially all of your business time and attention to the business of the Company, except for approved vacation periods and reasonable periods of illness or other incapacities permitted by the Company’s general employment policies. You shall perform such duties as are required by the Company’s Chief Executive Officer (“ CEO ”), to whom you will report. You represent to the Company that you are not subject to or a party to any employment agreement, non-competition covenant, or other agreement that would be breached by, or prohibit you from, executing this Agreement and performing fully your duties and responsibilities hereunder. Your primary work location shall be the Company’s office located in Orange County, California. The Company reserves the right to reasonably require you to perform your duties at places other than your primary office location from time to time, and to require reasonable business travel. The Company may modify your job title and duties as it deems necessary and appropriate in light of the Company’s needs and interests from time to time. 2. Compensation. 2.1 Base Salary. For services to be rendered hereunder, you shall receive a base salary at the rate of $700,000 per year (the “ Base Salary ”), subject to standard payroll deductions and withholdings and payable in accordance with the Company’s regular payroll schedule. 2.2 Annual Bonus. You will be eligible to receive an annual discretionary performance bonus with a target amount of up to 60% of your then current annual Base Salary (the “ Annual Bonus ”). You will be eligible to receive an Annual Bonus beginning with the 2027 performance year. For clarity, you will not be eligible to receive an Annual Bonus for 2026. Whether you receive an Annual Bonus for any given year, and the amount of any such Annual Bonus, will be determined by the Board of Directors of the Company and/or its Compensation Committee (the “ Board ”) in its sole discretion and will be based upon the achievement of corporate and/or individual objectives and milestones that are determined in the sole discretion of the Board. You must continue to be employed through the date the Annual Bonus is paid in order to earn such bonus. The Annual Bonus, if any, shall be paid to you in a lump sum no later than March 15 th of the calendar year that follows the performance year, subject to applicable payroll deductions and withholdings. 1. 2.3 Equity . (a) Stock Option . Subject to approval by the Board, you shall be granted an option (the “ Option ”) to purchase a number of shares of the Company’s Common Stock equal to 3% of the Company’s fully-diluted outstanding capital stock as of the date of grant, at an exercise price per share equal to the fair market value of a share of Common Stock on the date of grant, as determined by the Board. The Option shall vest over a four (4)-year period, with twenty-five percent (25%) of the shares subject to the Option vesting on the first anniversary of the Start Date and the remaining seventy-five percent (75%) vesting in substantially equal monthly installments over the thirty-six (36) months thereafter, in each case subject to your continued employment with the Company through the applicable vesting date. The Option shall be subject to the terms and conditions of the Vidya Therapeutics, Inc. 2027 Equity Incentive Plan (the “ Plan ”), as is expected to be approved and adopted by the Board, and the stock option agreement to be entered into between you and the Company, including the vesting schedule set forth therein. (b) Performance Award 1 . Subject to approval by the Board, you shall be granted an award of performance-based restricted stock units representing 0.5% of the Company’s fully-diluted outstanding capital stock as of the date of grant (the “ Performance Award 1 ”). Subject to your employment with the Company through the applicable vesting date, the Performance Award 1 shall become fully vested upon the earlier of: (i) the Company’s achievement of a thirty (30) trading day trailing average closing price per share of the Company’s Common Stock of at least $4.80 (the “ Performance Milestone 1 ”); or (ii) consummation of a Change in Control or Corporate Transaction (as defined in the Plan or the award agreement evidencing the Performance Award 1) in which the price payable per share of the Company’s Common Stock in connection with such Change in Control or Corporate Transaction, as determined by the Board in its sole discretion, is at least equal to $4.80 (each, a “ Milestone 1 Qualifying Transaction ”). The Performance Award 1 shall be deemed to have satisfied all performance conditions in full immediately prior to the effective time of a Milestone 1 Qualifying Transaction, contingent upon its consummation. The Performance Award 1 shall be subject to the terms and conditions of the Plan, as is expected to be approved and adopted by the Board, and the restricted stock unit award agreement to be entered into between you and the Company. Notwithstanding Section 6(c) of the Plan, any unsettled portion of the Performance Award 1 shall, subject to your employment through the applicable record date, vest and settle in shares immediately before, and in no event later than, the record date for such Milestone 1 Qualifying Transaction, so you are treated as a stockholder for all purposes of the transaction, subject to compliance with, or exemption from, Section 409A. Notwithstanding anything herein to the contrary, if your employment is terminated by the Company, the Performance Award 1 shall remain outstanding and eligible to vest for twelve (12) months following such termination, subject to your Continuous Service (as defined in the Plan), as a consultant or otherwise, with the Company through such date. 2. (c) Performance Award 2 . Subject to approval by the Board, you shall be granted an award of performance-based restricted stock units representing 0.5% of the Company’s fully-diluted outstanding capital stock as of the date of grant (the “ Performance Award 2 ”). Subject to your employment with the Company through the applicable vesting date, the Performance Award 2 shall become fully vested upon the earlier of: (i) the Company’s achievement of a thirty (30) trading day trailing average closing price per share of the Company’s Common Stock of at least $9.60 (the “ Performance Milestone 2 ”); or (ii) consummation of a Change in Control or Corporate Transaction in which the price payable per share of the Company’s Common Stock in connection with such Change in Control or Corporate Transaction, as determined by the Board in its sole discretion, is at least equal to $9.60 (each, a “ Milestone 2 Qualifying Transaction ”). The Performance Award 2 shall be deemed to have satisfied all performance conditions in full immediately prior to the effective time of a Milestone 2 Qualifying Transaction, contingent upon its consummation. The Performance Award 2 shall be subject to the terms and conditions of the Plan, as is expected to be approved and adopted by the Board, and the restricted stock unit award agreement to be entered into between you and the Company. Notwithstanding Section 6(c) of the Plan, any unsettled portion of the Performance Award 2 shall, subject to your employment through the applicable record date, vest and settle in shares immediately before, and in no event later than, the record date for such Milestone 2 Qualifying Transaction, so you are treated as a stockholder for all purposes of the transaction, subject to compliance with, or exemption from, Section 409A. Notwithstanding anything herein to the contrary, if your employment is terminated by the Company, the Performance Award 2 shall remain outstanding and eligible to vest for twelve (12) months following such termination, subject to your Continuous Service, as a consultant or otherwise, with the Company through such date. 3. Reasonable Business Expenses. You will be eligible for reimbursement of all reasonable, necessary, and documented out-of-pocket business, entertainment, and travel expenses incurred by you in connection with the performance of your duties hereunder in accordance with the Company's expense reimbursement policies and procedures. 4. Company Policies; Standard Company Benefits . The employment relationship between the parties shall be governed by the general employment policies and practices of the Company, except that when the terms of this Agreement differ from or are in conflict with the Company’s general employment policies or practices, this Agreement shall control. You shall be entitled to participate in all employee benefit programs for which you are eligible under the terms and conditions of the benefit plans that may be in effect from time to time and provided by the Company to its employees. The Company reserves the right to cancel or change the benefit plans or programs it offers to its employees at any time. 5. At-Will Employment. Your employment relationship is at-will. Either you or the Company may terminate the employment relationship at any time, with or without cause or advance notice. Upon termination of your employment for any reason, you shall resign from all positions and terminate any relationships as an employee, advisor, officer or director with the Company and any of its affiliates, each effective on the date of termination. 6. Outside Activities During Employment. Except with the prior written consent of the Board, you will not during the term of your employment with the Company undertake or engage in any other employment, occupation, or business enterprise, other than ones in which you are a passive investor. You may engage in civic and not-for-profit activities and serve as a director on the board of directors of up to two companies (in addition to the Company) so long as such activities do not materially interfere with the performance of your duties hereunder. You agree not to acquire, assume, or participate in, directly or indirectly, any position, investment or interest known to be adverse or antagonistic to the Company, its business or prospects, financial or otherwise. 3. 7. Termination; Severance. 7.1 Term and Termination. The term of this Agreement shall be the period commencing on the Start Date and ending on the date that this Agreement is terminated by either party pursuant to the provisions of this Agreement. You are employed at-will, meaning that, subject to the terms and conditions set forth herein, either the Company or you may terminate your employment at any time, with or without cause. 7.2 Compensation upon Termination. Upon the termination of your employment for any reason, the Company shall pay you all of your accrued and unpaid wages earned through your last day of employment (the “ Separation Date ”). 7.3 Severance and Change in Control Benefits. Following approval and adoption by the Board of Directors of a severance plan, you will be eligible to receive severance and change-in-control benefits consistent with those provided to similarly situated employees under such plan. Should the Company terminate your employment without Cause prior to approval and adoption of a severance plan, and provided that you remain in compliance with the terms of this Agreement (including the conditions described in Section 7.4 below), the Company shall provide you with the following benefits (the “ Severance Benefits ”): (a) Cash Severance. The Company shall pay you, as severance, the equivalent of twelve (12) months (the “ Severance Period ”) of your Base Salary in effect as of the Separation Date, subject to standard payroll deductions and withholdings (the “ Severance ”). The Severance will be paid as a continuation on the Company’s regular payroll, beginning no later than the first regularly-scheduled payroll date following the sixtieth (60 th ) day after your Separation Date, provided the Separation Agreement (as discussed in Section 7.4) has become effective. (b) Payment of Continued Group Health Plan Benefits. If you are eligible for and timely elect continued group health plan coverage under the Consolidated Omnibus Budget Reconciliation Act of 1985 or any state law of similar effect (“ COBRA ”) following your Separation Date, the Company will pay your COBRA group health insurance premiums for you and your eligible dependents directly to the insurer until the earliest of (A) the end of the period immediately following your Separation Date that is equal to the Severance Period (the “ COBRA Payment Period ”), (B) the expiration of your eligibility for continuation coverage under COBRA, or (C) the date when you become eligible for substantially equivalent health insurance coverage in connection with new employment or self-employment. For purposes of this Section, references to COBRA premiums shall not include any amounts payable by you under a Section 125 health care reimbursement plan under the Code. Notwithstanding the foregoing, if at any time the Company determines, in its sole discretion, that it cannot pay the COBRA premiums without potentially incurring financial costs or penalties under applicable law (including, without limitation, Section 2716 of the Public Health Service Act), then regardless of whether you elect continued health coverage under COBRA, and in lieu of providing the COBRA premiums, the Company will instead pay you on the last day of each remaining month of the COBRA Payment Period, a fully taxable cash payment equal to the COBRA premiums for that month, subject to applicable tax withholdings (such amount, the “ Special Severance Payment ”), which payments shall continue until the earlier of expiration of the COBRA Payment Period or the date when you become eligible for substantially equivalent health insurance coverage in connection with new employment or self-employment. On the first payroll date following the effectiveness of the Separation Agreement, the Company will make the first payment to the insurer under this clause (and, in the case of the Special Severance Payment, such payment will be to you, in a lump sum) equal to the aggregate amount of payments that the Company would have paid through such date had such payments instead commenced on the Separation Date, with the balance of the payments paid thereafter on the schedule described above. If you become eligible for coverage under another employer’s group health plan, you must immediately notify the Company of such event, and all payments and obligations under this subsection shall cease. 4. 7.4 Conditions to Receipt of Severance Benefits. The receipt of the Severance Benefits will be subject to you signing and not revoking a separation agreement and general release of claims in a form reasonably satisfactory to the Company (the “ Separation Agreement ”) by no later than the sixtieth (60th) day after the Separation Date (“ Release Deadline ”). No Severance Benefits will be paid or provided until the Separation Agreement becomes effective. You shall also resign from all positions and terminate any relationships as an employee, advisor, officer or director with the Company and any of its affiliates, each effective on the Separation Date. For purposes of this Agreement, “Cause” for termination has the meaning it has in the Plan. For clarity, following approval and adoption by the Board of Directors of a severance plan, you will no longer be eligible for severance under this Agreement. 8. Proprietary Information Obligations. As a condition of employment, you shall execute and abide by the Company’s standard form of Employee Confidential Information and Invention Assignment Agreement (the “ Confidentiality Agreement ”), attached as Exhibit A . In your work for the Company, you will be expected not to use or disclose any confidential information, including trade secrets, of any former employer or other person to whom you have an obligation of confidentiality. Rather, you will be expected to use only that information which is generally known and used by persons with training and experience comparable to your own, which is common knowledge in the industry or otherwise legally in the public domain, or which is otherwise provided or developed by the Company. You agree that you will not bring onto Company premises any unpublished documents or property belonging to any former employer or other person to whom you have an obligation of confidentiality. You hereby represent that you have disclosed to the Company any contract you have signed that may restrict your activities on behalf of the Company. 5. 9. Arbitration of All Disputes. To aid the rapid and economical resolution of disputes that may arise in connection with your employment with the Company, and in exchange for the mutual promises contained in this Agreement, you and the Company agree that any and all disputes, claims, or causes of action, in law or equity, including but not limited to statutory claims, arising from or relating to the enforcement, breach, performance, or interpretation of this Agreement, your employment with the Company, or the termination of your employment, shall be resolved, to the fullest extent permitted by law, by final, binding and confidential arbitration conducted by JAMS, Inc. (“ JAMS ”) or its successor, under JAMS’ then applicable rules and procedures appropriate to the relief being sought (available upon request and also currently available at the following web address: (i) https://www.jamsadr.com/rules-employment-arbitration/ and (ii) https://www.jamsadr.com/rules-comprehensive-arbitration/) at a location closest to where you last worked for the Company or another mutually agreeable location. Notwithstanding the foregoing, if JAMS is unavailable due to location or otherwise, or if the parties mutually agree, then the arbitration shall be conducted by the American Arbitration Association (“ AAA ”) or its successor, under AAA’s then applicable rules and procedures appropriate to the relief being sought (available upon request and also currently available at the following web address: https://www.adr.org/sites/default/files/EmploymentRules-Web.pdf), at a location closest to where you last worked for the Company or another mutually agreeable location. Any demand for arbitration must be made within the statute of limitations applicable to the claim asserted as if such claim were asserted in court. Failure to demand arbitration (or, where applicable, file a counterclaim, crossclaim, or third-party claim) within such time limitation shall serve as a waiver and release with respect to all such claims. You acknowledge that by agreeing to this arbitration procedure, both you and the Company waive the right to resolve any such dispute through a trial by jury or judge. The Federal Arbitration Act, 9 U.S.C. § 1 et seq., will, to the fullest extent permitted by law, govern the interpretation and enforcement of this arbitration agreement and any arbitration proceedings. This provision shall not be mandatory for any claim or cause of action to the extent applicable law prohibits subjecting such claim or cause of action to mandatory arbitration and such applicable law is not preempted by the Federal Arbitration Act or otherwise invalid (collectively, the “ Excluded Claims ”), such as non-individual claims that cannot be waived under applicable law, claims or causes of action alleging sexual harassment or a nonconsensual sexual act or sexual contact, or unemployment or workers’ compensation claims brought before the applicable state governmental agency. In the event you or the Company intend to bring multiple claims, including one of the Excluded Claims listed above, the Excluded Claims may be filed with a court, while any other claims will remain subject to mandatory arbitration. You acknowledge and agree that proceedings of any non-individual claim(s) under the California Private Attorneys General Act (“ PAGA ”) that may be brought in court shall be stayed for the duration and pending a final resolution of the arbitration of any individual or individual PAGA claim. Nothing herein prevents you from filing and pursuing proceedings before a federal or state governmental agency, although if you choose to pursue a claim following the exhaustion of any applicable administrative remedies, that claim would be subject to this provision. In addition, with the exception of Excluded Claims arising out of 9 U.S.C. § 401 et seq., all claims, disputes, or causes of action under this section, whether by you or the Company, must be brought in an individual capacity, and shall not be brought as a plaintiff (or claimant) or class member in any purported class, representative, or collective proceeding, nor joined or consolidated with the claims of any other person or entity. You acknowledge that by agreeing to this arbitration procedure, both you and the Company waive all rights to have any dispute be brought, heard, administered, resolved, or arbitrated on a class, representative, or collective action basis. The arbitrator may not consolidate the claims of more than one person or entity, and may not preside over any form of representative or class proceeding. If a court finds, by means of a final decision, not subject to any further appeal or recourse, that the preceding sentences regarding class, representative, or collective claims or proceedings violate applicable law or are otherwise found unenforceable as to a particular claim or request for relief, the parties agree that any such claim(s) or request(s) for relief be severed from the arbitration and may proceed in a court of law rather than by arbitration. All other claims or requests for relief shall be arbitrated. You will have the right to be represented by legal counsel at any arbitration proceeding. Questions of whether a claim is subject to arbitration and procedural questions which grow out of the dispute and bear on the final disposition are matters for the arbitrator to decide, provided however, that if required by applicable law, a court and not the arbitrator may determine the enforceability of this paragraph with respect to Excluded Claims. The arbitrator shall: (a) have the authority to compel adequate discovery for the resolution of the dispute and to award such relief as would otherwise be permitted by law; and (b) issue a written statement signed by the arbitrator regarding the disposition of each claim and the relief, if any, awarded as to each claim, the reasons for the award, and the arbitrator’s essential findings and conclusions on which the award is based. The arbitrator shall be authorized to award all relief that you or the Company would be entitled to seek in a court of law. The Company shall pay all arbitration administrative fees in excess of the administrative fees that you would be required to pay if the dispute were decided in a court of law. Each party is responsible for its own attorneys’ fees, except as may be expressly set forth in your Employee Confidential Information and Inventions Assignment Agreement or as otherwise provided under applicable law. Nothing in this Agreement is intended to prevent either you or the Company from obtaining injunctive relief in court to prevent irreparable harm pending the conclusion of any such arbitration. Any awards or orders in such arbitrations may be entered and enforced as judgments in the federal and state courts of any competent jurisdiction. 6. 10. General Provisions. This Agreement, together with the Confidentiality Agreement, constitutes the entire agreement between you and the Company with regard to this subject matter and is the complete, final, and exclusive embodiment of the parties’ agreement with regard to this subject matter. This Agreement is entered into without reliance on any promise or representation, written or oral, other than those expressly contained herein, and it supersedes any other such promises, warranties, or representations. Modifications or amendments to this Agreement, other than those changes expressly reserved to the Company’s discretion in this Agreement, must be made in a written agreement signed by you and the Company’s Chief Executive Officer. Whenever possible, each provision of this Agreement will be interpreted in such manner as to be effective and valid under applicable law, but if any provision of this Agreement is held to be invalid, illegal or unenforceable in any respect under any applicable law or rule in any jurisdiction, such invalidity, illegality or unenforceability will not affect any other provision or any other jurisdiction, but this Agreement will be reformed, construed and enforced in such jurisdiction to the extent possible in keeping with the intent of the parties. Any waiver of any breach of any provisions of this Agreement must be in writing to be effective, and it shall not thereby be deemed to have waived any preceding or succeeding breach of the same or any other provision of this Agreement. This Agreement is intended to bind and inure to the benefit of and be enforceable by you and the Company, and their respective successors, assigns, heirs, executors, and administrators. The Company may freely assign this Agreement, without your prior written consent. You may not assign any of your duties hereunder and you may not assign any of your rights hereunder without the written consent of the Company. This Agreement shall become effective as of the Start Date and shall terminate upon your termination of employment with the Company. The obligations as set forth under Sections 8, 9, and 10 will survive the termination of your employment and this Agreement. All questions concerning the construction, validity and interpretation of this Agreement will be governed by the laws of the State of California. This offer is subject to satisfactory proof of your identity and right to work in the United States and other applicable pre-employment screenings. 7. We look forward to having you join us. If you have any questions about this Agreement, please do not hesitate to call me. Best regards, Processa Pharmaceuticals, Inc. /s/ Sheila Gujrathi Sheila Gujrathi, MD On Behalf of the Board of Directors of Processa Pharmaceuticals, Inc. Accepted and agreed: /s/ Gregory J. Flesher Gregory J. Flesher Date: November 3, 2026 8.

text: EX-10.2 2 ex_1036976.htm EXHIBIT 10.2 ex_1036976.htm Exhibit 10.2 Senior Secured Promissory Note SENIOR SECURED PROMISSORY NOTE Principal Sum: $1,750,000.00 Dated: October 27, 2026 FOR VALUE RECEIVED, To Be Brands, LLC (“ Borrower ”), a North Carolina limited liability company with an address at 10130 Perimeter Parkway, Charlotte, NC 28216 (“ Borrower ’ s Address ”), together with each of its undersigned subsidiaries (the “ Borrower Subsidiaries ”), namely: (i) ISI Brands Inc. (“ ISI ”), (ii) InnoVitamin Organics, LLC (“ IO ”), (iii) Reserve Life Organics, LLC (“ RLO ”), and (iv) ResVitale, LLC (“ ResVitale ”), hereby promises to pay Akretive Holdings, LLC (“ Lender ”), a Nevada limited liability company with an address at P.O. Box 1447, Franklin, Tennessee 37065 (“ Lender ’ s Address ”), the principal sum of $1,750,000.00 in United States currency (the “ Principal Sum ”) and accrued interest on or before the maturity date that is two (2) years from the date of issuance of this Note as set forth above (the “ Maturity Date ”). 1. Limitation of Liability . For the avoidance of doubt, no amounts owed to Lender hereunder shall be owed by, and no obligation under this Note shall attach to or be enforceable against: (a) Philip J. Von Kahle in his capacity as the duly appointed assignee for the benefit of creditors of Twinlab Consolidation Corporation, Twinlab Holdings, Inc., and Organic Holdings LLC (the “Assignee”), either in his representative or individual capacity; (b) the assignment estates of Twinlab Consolidation Corporation, Twinlab Holdings, Inc., and Organic Holdings LLC (collectively, the “Assignors” and their respective assignment estates, the “Estates”); (c) any of the Assignors; (d) Twinlab Consolidated Holdings, Inc. (“Twinlab”); or (e) any subsidiary of any Assignor or of Twinlab whose equity interests are not Acquired Assets under that certain Asset Purchase Agreement dated as of September 1, 2026 (the “ APA ”), including without limitation Twinlab Corporation, NutraScience Labs, Inc., NutraScience Labs IP Corporation, Reserve Life Nutrition, LLC, CocoaWell, LLC, Re-Body, LLC, Fembody, LLC, Organics Management LLC, Joie Essance, LLC, and Innovita Specialty Distribution LLC (collectively, the “Excluded Entities”). This Note is the sole obligation of the Borrower and the Borrower Subsidiaries, as provided in Section 3.1(e) of the APA. 2. Interest . (a) Interest payable hereunder shall commence accruing on the date of issuance through the Maturity Date, at an interest rate equal to Nine Percent (9%) per annum and shall be due and payable in arrears on the first (1st) day of each month during the term of this note and on the Maturity Date. The Principal Sum and accrued interest may be prepaid, in whole or in part, at any time prior to the Maturity Date, without penalty. (b) Any amount representing the Principal Sum, either in part or in whole, that is not paid on the Maturity Date shall bear interest at a simple interest rate equal to Eighteen Percent (18%) per annum and be due and payable in arrears on the first (1st) day of each month after the Maturity Date and upon final payment of the Principal Sum. (c) In no event shall interest payable hereunder be compounded or exceed the maximum rate or amount permitted by applicable law. The Principal Sum and all interest accrued thereon are payable to Lender at Lender’s Address or to such other nominee, address, or bank coordinates as Lender may direct by written notice to Borrower at Borrower’s Address. Page 1 of 4 Senior Secured Promissory Note 3. Security Agreement . Borrower and Lender acknowledge that this note is entered into upon condition that each such party has entered into and fully executed a Senior Security Agreement referencing this Note and dated as of October 27, 2026, which shall remain binding and in effect according to its terms (the “ Security Agreement ”). 4. Events of Default . Borrower’s failure to abide by or comply with or make any payment due under the terms of this note or the Security Agreement shall be deemed an “ Event of Default ”. Upon the occurrence of any Event of Default, Lender may exercise any rights and or remedies against Borrower under the Security Agreement, including, without limitation, the acceleration of amounts owed, the exercise of any rights extended under the Security Agreement or otherwise, and/or the commencement of a legal action against Borrower for amounts owed hereunder. 5. Interpretation . In the event of any discrepancy or question of interpretation concerning this note or the Security Agreement, the terms and interpretation of the Security Agreement shall govern and control the terms and interpretation of this note. 6. Jury Trial; Governing Law; Jurisdiction . Borrower and Lender hereby waive trial by jury in any action, proceeding, or counterclaim brought by any party hereto or any beneficiary hereof on any matter whatsoever arising out of or in any way connected with this note. Borrower and Lender agree that this note will be governed by, construed, and enforced in accordance with, and subject to, the laws of the State of Nevada , except with respect to the choice of law provisions thereof. Borrower and Lender hereby submit to the jurisdiction and venue of the state and federal courts located in the State of Nevada for purposes of any arbitration or litigation related to this note. 7. Counterparts . This note may be executed in any number of counterparts, each of which, when taken together, will be deemed to be an original and one and the same instrument. This note will not become effective until all counterparts hereof have been duly executed by all parties hereto. 8. Right to Counsel . Lender hereby acknowledges that it has been advised of its right to retain independent legal counsel in connection with the negotiation, legal effect, and meaning of this note and all of the documents referenced and incorporated herein, and Lender either has retained independent legal counsel or knowingly and voluntarily waived such right. 9. Relationship to APA . This Note is a Transaction Document under, and is entered into pursuant to the APA. Capitalized terms used but not defined herein shall have the meanings ascribed to them in the APA. In the event of any conflict or inconsistency between the terms of the APA and the terms of this Note, the terms of the APA shall govern. text: EX-10.3 3 ex_1036977.htm EXHIBIT 10.3 ex_1036977.htm Exhibit 10.3 Senior Security Agreement SENIOR SECURITY AGREEMENT This Senior Security Agreement (this “ Security Agreement ”) is effective as of October 27, 2026 (the “ Effective Date ”), by and between To Be Brands, LLC (“ Borrower ”), a North Carolina limited liability company, together with each of its undersigned subsidiaries, namely: (i) ISI Brands Inc. (“ ISI ”), (ii) InnoVitamin Organics, LLC (“ IO ”), (iii) Reserve Life Organics, LLC (“ RLO ”), and (iv) ResVitale, LLC (“ ResVitale ”) (each a “ Borrower Subsidiary ” and collectively the “ Borrower Subsidiaries ”), and Akretive Holdings, LLC, a Nevada limited liability company (“ Lender ”). WHEREAS, Borrower has issued a Senior Secured Promissory Note to Lender in the principal amount of One Million Seven Hundred Fifty Thousand Dollars and 00/100 Cents ( $1,750,000.00 ), dated as of the Effective Date (the “ Note ”). WHEREAS, Lender has required, as a condition of accepting said Note, that Borrower execute this Security Agreement to secure the repayment of the obligations of Borrower under the Note. NOW THEREFORE, in consideration of the foregoing recitals, and other good and valuable consideration, the receipt and sufficiency of which is hereby acknowledged, Borrower hereby agrees as follows: 1. Liability Secured . This Security Agreement is entered into as security for repayment of the Note executed by the same parties hereto and on the same date hereon. 2. Granting Clause . As security for the obligations under the Note and every extension or renewal thereof, Borrower does hereby grant, pledge, convey, and deliver to Lender a security interest in all of the right, title, and interest of Borrower, in and to the personal property set forth below and referred to herein as the “ Collateral ”. 3. Collateral . All of the following personal property shall be deemed “Collateral” for purposes of this Security Agreement: (a) all of Borrower’s right, title, and interest in and to that certain personal property set forth on Schedule A attached hereto and incorporated herein; and (b) all proceeds and replacements of the foregoing. For the avoidance of doubt, Collateral shall not include any assets (including equity interests in entities) belonging to (i) Philip J. Von Kahle in his capacity as the duly appointed assignee for the benefit of creditors of Twinlab Consolidation Corporation, Twinlab Holdings, Inc., and Organic Holdings LLC (the “ Assignee ”) or (ii) the assignment estates of Twinlab Consolidation Corporation, Twinlab Holdings, Inc., and Organic Holdings LLC (collectively, the “ Assignors ” and their respective assignment estates, the “ Estates ”). Notwithstanding anything in this Security Agreement to the contrary, no obligation under this Security Agreement shall attach to or be enforceable against: (a) the Assignee (in his representative or individual capacity), (b) the Estates, (c) any Assignor, (d) Twinlab Consolidated Holdings, Inc. (“ Twinlab ”); or (e) any subsidiary of any Assignor or of Twinlab whose equity interests are not Acquired Assets under that certain Asset Purchase Agreement dated as of September 1, 2026 (the “ APA ”), including without limitation Twinlab Corporation, NutraScience Labs, Inc., NutraScience Labs IP Corporation, Reserve Life Nutrition, LLC, CocoaWell, LLC, Re-Body, LLC, Fembody, LLC, Organics Management LLC, Joie Essance, LLC, and Innovita Specialty Distribution LLC (collectively, the “ Excluded Entities ”). This Security Agreement is the sole obligation of the Borrower and the Borrower Subsidiaries, as provided in Section 3.1(e) of the APA. Page 1 of 6 Senior Security Agreement 4. Transfer Restrictions; Impairments . Without the prior written consent of Lender, Borrower shall not, and shall not permit any Borrower Subsidiary or any direct or indirect subsidiary of Borrower to: (a) Asset Transfers. Sell, assign, transfer, lease, license, contribute, convey, or otherwise dispose of any material assets, properties, rights, or interests, whether tangible or intangible, other than (i) sales of inventory in the ordinary course of business consistent with past practice, (ii) dispositions of obsolete or worn-out equipment in the ordinary course of business, or (iii) other dispositions expressly approved in writing by Lender. (b) Equity Transfers and Issuances. Issue, sell, transfer, redeem, repurchase, or otherwise dispose of any equity interests of any Borrower Subsidiary, or permit any dilution of the ownership interests of Borrower or any Borrower Subsidiary, except (i) transfers among wholly owned subsidiaries of Borrower, (ii) issuances approved in writing by Lender, or (iii) equity issuances made by Borrower itself that do not impair the Collateral. (c) Extraordinary Transactions. Enter into any merger, consolidation, recapitalization, restructuring, joint venture, dissolution, winding up, or similar transaction that would reasonably be expected to materially impair the value of the Collateral. (d) New Subsidiaries. Neither Borrower nor any Borrower Subsidiary shall create or acquire any subsidiary unless such subsidiary becomes a guarantor and grants a security interest in its assets and equity interests to Lender pursuant to an amendment or addendum to this Agreement. (e) Impairments. Except as expressly set forth in Section 6 below (headed “Rights of Subordination”) Borrower shall not authorize, permit, or allow any other direct or indirect pledge, lien, encumbrance, or other impairment of any Collateral, including, but not limited to those arising under any obligation of any parent entity of Borrower. 5. Warranties of Title . Borrower hereby: (a) covenants with Lender and its successors and assigns that Borrower is the lawful owner of the Collateral and has the right to sell, assign, convey, and grant a security interest in the same and that the Collateral is free and clear of all encumbrances and security interests (other than that of Lender and any other security interest that is subordinated to Lender); (b) warrants and covenants to forever defend the title of the Collateral unto Lender and his successors and assigns against the claims of all persons whomsoever, whether lawful or unlawful; (c) warrants that, to Borrower’s knowledge, no senior financing statement covering any of the Collateral or any proceeds therefrom is on file at any public office; and (d) agrees, promptly upon request from Lender to join with Lender in executing one or more financing statements pursuant to the Uniform Commercial Code of the applicable state in a form satisfactory to Lender and to pay the cost of filing the same in all public offices wherever filing is deemed necessary or prudent by Lender. For clarity, Lender shall have the right, from time to time and at any time, to prepare, execute, and file one or more financing statements and amendments thereto pursuant to the Uniform Commercial Code of the applicable state in a form satisfactory to Lender without any further authorization from Borrower or any Borrower Subsidiary, and upon prior written notice to Borrower, which cost will be fully reimbursed to Lender by Borrower and each Borrower Subsidiary, with joint and several liability therefor. Page 2 of 6 Senior Security Agreement 6. Rights of Subordination . Lender acknowledges that from time-to-time Borrower may require additional working capital for the benefit of Borrower and Borrower Subsidiaries. In the event Borrower enters into a credit facility for working capital with a lender (a “ Working Capital Facility ”), (a) the Working Capital Facility shall rank senior to the Note and any amounts due under the Note, (b) the security interest granted hereunder shall be subordinate to any security interest granted to secure such Working Capital Facility, and (c) Lender shall, upon Borrower’s reasonable request, execute and deliver such agreements or other documents as may be reasonably required by the working capital lender to effectuate the foregoing. 7. Limitations on Rights of Subordination . Notwithstanding any other provision of this Agreement, Borrower and Borrower Subsidiaries shall be prohibited from granting any security interest in any Collateral other than financial accounts, accounts receivable, letter of credit rights, and similar rights to payment, whether any of the foregoing is now owned or later acquired, for any reason whatsoever, without the prior written consent of Lender. For clarity, no Collateral in the form of intellectual properties or tangible assets of any kind shall be pledged, liened, or encumbered by Borrower, any Borrower Subsidiary, or any parent company of Borrower. At no point in time prior to the full satisfaction of Borrower’s obligations under the Note and this Security Agreement shall Borrower enter into more than one Working Capital Facility that creates a security interest that is senior in creditor priority to the security interest created by this Security Agreement at any single point in time. 8. Taxes and Assessments . Borrower agrees to pay all taxes, rents, assessments, and charges levied against the Collateral and all other claims that are or may become liens against the Collateral, or any part thereof, and should default be made in the payment of the same, Lender, at its option, may pay the same; provided, however, that Borrower may contest in good faith by appropriate proceedings any such taxes, assessments, or claims so long as adequate reserves are maintained. Notwithstanding the foregoing, Lender may, at any time, in Lender’s sole discretion, pay any unpaid or contested taxes, assessments, or claims to preserve and prevent any impairment to the Collateral, and Lender reserves all rights to seek reimbursement and indemnity therefor from Borrower if such contest is not fully resolved in favor of Borrower. 9. Non-Waiver . It is agreed that no delay in exercising any right or option given or granted hereby to Lender shall be construed as a waiver thereof; nor shall a single or partial exercise of any other right, power, or privilege. Lender may permit Borrower to remedy any default without waiving the default so remedied, and Lender may waive any default without waiving any other subsequent or prior default by Borrower. 10. Events of Default . As used in this Security Agreement, the term “ Event of Default ” means the occurrence of a violation or default in the observance or performance of any term, agreement, covenant, condition, or stipulation contained or referred to in this Security Agreement or the occurrence of an “Event of Default” under the Note; provided, however, that no Event of Default shall be deemed to have occurred under this Security Agreement unless: (i) with respect to a failure to make any payment when due under the Note, such failure continues for ten (10) business days after written notice thereof from Lender to Borrower; or (ii) with respect to a failure to comply with any other term or condition of the Note or this Security Agreement, such failure is material and continues for thirty (30) days after written notice thereof from Lender to Borrower. For purposes of this Agreement, the term “ business day ” means any day of the week other than weekends and U.S. Federal holidays. Page 3 of 6 Senior Security Agreement 11. Acceleration of Liabilities . Upon the occurrence of any uncured Event of Default, Lender shall have the right to declare the entire unpaid balance of the Note immediately due and payable by written notice to Borrower. 12. Lender ’ s Rights After an Event of Default . Upon the occurrence of an Event of Default that remains uncured after any applicable notice and cure period, Lender shall have, in addition to any other rights under this Security Agreement or under applicable law, the right upon not less than ten (10) business days’ prior written notice to Borrower to take any or all of the following actions at the same or different times: (a) to collect all or any part of the Collateral defined herein and take control of any cash or non-cash proceeds of Collateral; (b) to enforce payment of any Collateral, to prosecute any action or proceeding with respect to the Collateral, to extend the time of payment of any and all Collateral, to make allowance and adjustments with respect thereto, and to issue credits in the name of Borrower; and (c) to exercise, in addition to all other rights and remedies of a Lender upon default under the Uniform Commercial Code of the applicable state or any state. The net cash proceeds resulting from the exercise of any of the foregoing rights, after deducting all reasonable and documented charges, expenses, costs, and attorneys’ fees relating thereto, including any and all reasonable costs and expenses incurred in securing the possession of Collateral and preparing the same for sale, shall be applied by Lender to any payments due under the Note, in any order that Lender may determine or choose, and Borrower shall remain liable to Lender for any deficiency remaining thereafter. Notwithstanding the foregoing, Lender shall have the right to participate in any Collateral auction and bid the price of any sale of Collateral up to the full amount of any outstanding liability owed by Borrower to Lender and take clear, unencumbered title to and control over the Collateral in lieu of a cash sale that would result in insufficient proceeds to satisfy the entirety of such outstanding liability owing to Lender under the Note and this Security Agreement. Lender shall conduct any sale of the Collateral in a commercially reasonable manner. 13. Term and Termination . This Security Agreement shall continue in full force and effect until all obligations of Borrower to Lender pursuant to the Note have been fully satisfied and extinguished in accordance with the terms and conditions of the Note and this Security Agreement. Upon full satisfaction of all such obligations and at Borrower’s written request and expense, Lender shall promptly execute and deliver to Borrower all UCC-3 termination statements and such other documents as may be reasonably necessary to release Lender’s security interest in the Collateral. 14. Borrower Subsidiary Obligations . All rights of Lender against Borrower pursuant to this Agreement shall be joint and several obligations of each Borrower Subsidiary (and each additional subsidiary of Borrower or a Borrower Subsidiary formed after the Effective Date) to Lender on a pari passu basis with Borrower. Page 4 of 6 Senior Security Agreement 15. Successors and Assigns . All covenants and agreements herein made by Borrower shall bind it and its respective successors and assigns, and every option, right, and privilege herein reserved or granted to Lender shall inure to the benefit of and may be exercised by Lender’s successors or assigns; provided that Lender shall provide Borrower with prompt written notice of any assignment of this Security Agreement or the Note. 16. Modification; Amendment; Waiver . No modification, amendment, or waiver of any provision of this Security Agreement, any note secured hereby, nor consent to any departure by Borrower therefrom shall in any event be effective unless the same shall be in writing and signed by Lender and Borrower, and then such waiver or consent shall be effective only in the specific instance and for the purpose for which given. 17. Notices . Any request, demand, or notice provided in this Security Agreement to be given by either party hereto to the other shall be conclusively deemed to have been given when the same shall have been deposited in the United States mail, postage prepaid, addressed to the party to whom such request, demand, or notice is directed, at the following address, or delivered by hand to such party at such address: (a) if to Borrowers, to: 10130 Perimeter Parkway, Charlotte, NC 28216 and (b) if to Lender, to: P.O. Box 1447, Franklin, Tennessee 37065. 18. Governing Law; Venue . This Security Agreement shall be construed in accordance with and governed by the laws of the State of Nevada , without regard to the conflicts of laws principles thereof, and any claim arising hereunder shall be brought in the state or federal courts located in the State of Nevada . 19. Interpretation . In the event of any discrepancy or question of interpretation concerning this Security Agreement or the Note, the terms and interpretation of this Security Agreement shall govern and control the terms and interpretation of the Note. 20. Counterparts. This Security Agreement may be executed in any number of counterparts, each of which, when taken together, will be deemed to be an original and one and the same instrument. This Security Agreement will not become effective until all counterparts hereof have been duly executed by all parties hereto. 21. Independent Legal Counsel. Each party hereby acknowledges that it has been advised of its right to retain independent legal counsel in connection with the negotiation, legal effect, and meaning of this Security Agreement and all of the documents referenced and incorporated herein, and each party either has retained independent legal counsel or knowingly and voluntarily waived such right. 22. Relationship to APA . This Security Agreement is a Transaction Document under, and is entered into pursuant to, the APA. Capitalized terms used but not defined herein shall have the meanings ascribed to them in the APA. In the event of any conflict or inconsistency between the terms of the APA and the terms of this Security Agreement, the terms of the APA shall govern.
