Except as provided in this Section 10, a Participant shall have no rights by reason of (i) any subdivision or consolidation of shares of stock of any class, (ii) the payment of any dividend or (iii) any other increase or decrease in the number of 9 shares of stock of any class. Any issuance by the Company of shares of stock of any class, or securities convertible into shares of stock of any class, shall not affect, and no adjustment by reason thereof shall be made with respect to, the number or exercise price of Shares subject to an Award. The grant of an Award pursuant to the Plan shall not affect in any way the right or power of the Company to make adjustments, reclassifications, reorganizations or changes of its capital or business structure, to merge or consolidate or to dissolve, liquidate, sell or transfer all or any part of its business or assets. 11. Compliance with Section 409A . Unless otherwise expressly set forth in an Award Agreement, it is intended that awards granted under the Plan shall be exempt from Section 409A of the Code, and any ambiguity in the terms of an Award Agreement and the Plan shall be interpreted consistently with this intent. To the extent an award is not exempt from Section 409A of the Code (any such award, a “409A Award”), any ambiguity in the terms of such award and the Plan shall be interpreted in a manner that to the maximum extent permissible supports the award’s compliance with the requirements of that statute. Notwithstanding anything to the contrary permitted under the Plan, in no event shall a modification of an Award not already subject to Section 409A of the Code be given effect if such modification would cause the Award to become subject to Section 409A of the Code unless the parties explicitly acknowledge and consent to the modification as one having that effect. A 409A Award shall be subject to such additional rules and requirements as specified by the Board from time to time in order for it to comply with the requirements of Section 409A of the Code. In this regard, if any amount under a 409A Award is payable upon a “separation from service” to an individual who is considered a “specified employee” (as each term is defined under Section 409A of the Code), then no such payment shall be made prior to the date that is the earlier of (i) six months and one day after the Participant’s separation from service or (ii) the Participant’s death, but only to the extent such delay is necessary to prevent such payment from being subject to Section 409A(a)(1). In addition, if a Change in Control constitutes a payment event with respect to any 409A Award, then the transaction with respect to such award must also constitute a “change in control event” as defined in Treasury Regulation Section 1.409A-3(i)(5) to the extent required by Section 409A of the Code. Neither the Company nor any member of the Board shall have any liability to a Participant in the event an Award held by the Participant fails to achieve its intended characterization under applicable tax law. 12. Withholding Taxes . To the extent required by Applicable Law, a Participant shall be required to satisfy, in a manner satisfactory to the Company or Subsidiary, as applicable, any withholding tax obligations that arise by reason of a Stock Option or Stock Appreciation Right exercise, the vesting of or settlement of Shares under an Award, an election pursuant to Section 83(b) of the Code or otherwise with respect to an Award. Neither the Company nor any of its Subsidiaries shall be required to issue or deliver Shares, make any payment or to recognize the transfer or disposition of Shares until such obligations are satisfied. The Board may permit or require applicable tax withholding obligations to be satisfied by having the Company withhold a portion of the Shares that otherwise would be issued or delivered to a Participant upon exercise of a Stock Option or Stock Appreciation Right or upon the vesting or settlement of an Award, or by tendering Shares previously acquired, provided that in no event shall the Fair Market Value of any Shares withheld to satisfy tax withholding obligations with respect to an Award exceed the 10 taxes required to be withheld based on the maximum statutory tax rates in the applicable taxing jurisdictions. Any such elections are subject to such conditions or procedures as may be established by the Board and may be subject to disapproval by the Board. 13. Duration and Amendments; Stockholder Approval . a. Term of the Plan . The Plan shall terminate automatically 10 years after the Restatement Date. The Plan may be terminated on any earlier date pursuant to Subsection (b) below. b. Right to Amend or Terminate the Plan . The Board may amend, suspend or terminate the Plan at any time and for any reason. Stockholder approval shall not be necessary for any amendment to the Plan, except to the extent stockholder approval is required by Applicable Law (including such stockholder approval as may be required to authorize grant of Incentive Stock Options to Employees or as may be required under stock exchange listing standards). c. Effect of Amendment or Termination . No Shares shall be issued or sold and no Award granted under the Plan after the termination of the Plan, except upon exercise of a Stock Option, Stock Appreciation Right (or any other right to purchase Shares) or settlement of any other Award granted under the Plan prior to such termination. Except as otherwise provided in Sections 10 or 13(d), which specifically do not require the consent of any Participant, no termination, amendment, suspension, or modification of the Plan or an Award Agreement shall adversely affect in any material way any Award previously granted under the Plan, without the written consent of the Participant of such Award; provided that the Board may modify an Incentive Stock Option to disqualify such Stock Option from treatment as an “incentive stock option” under Section 422 of the Code without the Participant’s consent. d. Adjustments to Outstanding Awards . The Board may in its sole discretion at any time, including in connection with a Change in Control, and without the consent of any Participant, (i) provide that all or a portion of a Participant’s Stock Options, Stock Appreciation Rights and other Awards in the nature of rights that may be exercised shall become fully or partially exercisable; (ii) provide that all or a part of the time-based vesting restrictions on all or a portion of the outstanding Awards shall lapse, and/or that any Performance Objectives or other performance-based criteria with respect to any Awards shall be deemed to be wholly or partially satisfied; or (iii) waive any other limitation or requirement under any such Award, in each case, as of such date as the Board may, in its sole discretion, declare. e. Prohibition on Repricing . Except for adjustments made pursuant to Section 10, the Board or the Committee will not, without the further approval of the stockholders of the Company, authorize the amendment of any outstanding Stock Option or Stock Appreciation Right to reduce the exercise price. No Stock Option or Stock Appreciation Right will be cancelled and replaced with an Award having a lower exercise price, or for another Award, or for cash without further approval of the stockholders of the Company, except as provided in Section 10. Furthermore, no Stock Option or Stock Appreciation Right will provide for the payment, at the time of exercise, of a cash bonus or grant or sale of another Award 11 without further approval of the stockholders of the Company. This Section 13(e) is intended to prohibit the repricing of “underwater” Stock Options or Stock Appreciation Rights without stockholder approval and will not be construed to prohibit the adjustments provided for in Section 10. 14. Miscellaneous . a. Securities Law Requirements . Shares shall not be issued under the Plan unless, in the opinion of counsel acceptable to the Board, the issuance and delivery of such Shares comply with (or are exempt from) all applicable requirements of law, including (without limitation) the Securities Act, the rules and regulations promulgated thereunder, state securities laws and regulations, and the regulations of any stock exchange or other securities market on which the Company’s securities may then be traded. The Company shall not be liable for a failure to issue Shares as a result of such requirements. Unless and until the Shares have been registered under the Securities Act, each certificate evidencing any Shares delivered pursuant to the Plan, if any, shall bear a restrictive legend in a form specified by the Company. b. No Right of Continued Employment or Service . The Plan shall not confer upon any Participant any right with respect to continuance of employment or other service with the Company or any Subsidiary, nor shall it interfere in any way with any right the Company or any Subsidiary would otherwise have to terminate such Participant’s employment or other service at any time. No Employee, Director or Consultant shall have the right to be selected to receive an Award under the Plan, or, having been so selected, to be selected to receive future Awards. c. Unfunded, Unsecured Plan . Neither a Participant nor any other person shall, by reason of participation in the Plan, acquire any right or title to any assets, funds or property of the Company or any Subsidiary, including, without limitation, any specific funds, assets or other property which the Company or any Subsidiary may set aside in anticipation of any liability under the Plan. A Participant shall have only a contractual right to an Award or the amounts, if any, payable under the Plan, unsecured by any assets of the Company or any Subsidiary, and nothing contained in the Plan shall constitute a guarantee that the assets of the Company or any Subsidiary shall be sufficient to pay any benefits to any person. d. Severability . If any provision of the Plan is or becomes invalid, illegal or unenforceable in any jurisdiction, or would disqualify the Plan or any Award under any law deemed applicable by the Board, such provision shall be construed or deemed amended or limited in scope to conform to Applicable Law or, in the discretion of the Board, it shall be stricken and the remainder of the Plan shall remain in full force and effect. e. Acceptance of the Plan . By accepting any benefit under the Plan, each Participant and each person claiming under or through any such Participant shall be conclusively deemed to have indicated their acceptance and ratification of, and consent to, all of the terms and conditions of the Plan and any action taken under the Plan by the Board or the Company, in any case in accordance with the terms and conditions of the Plan. 12 f. Successors . All obligations of the Company under the Plan and with respect to Awards shall be binding on any successor to the Company, whether the existence of such successor is the result of a direct or indirect purchase, merger, consolidation, or other event, or a sale or disposition of all or substantially all of the business and/or assets of the Company and references to the “Company” herein and in any Award Agreements shall be deemed to refer to such successors. g. Applicable Law . The obligations of the Company with respect to Awards under the Plan shall be subject to all Applicable Laws and such approvals by any governmental agencies as the Committee determines may be required. The Plan and each Award Agreement shall be governed by the laws of the State of Delaware, excluding any conflicts or choice of law rule or principle that might otherwise refer construction or interpretation of the Plan to the substantive law of another jurisdiction. 15. Definitions . As used in the Plan, the following definitions shall apply: “Applicable Law” means the applicable requirements relating to the administration of equity-based compensation plans under U.S. state corporate laws, U.S. federal and state securities laws, the Code, the rules of any stock exchange or quotation system on which the Shares are listed or quoted and the applicable laws of any other country or jurisdiction where Awards are granted under the Plan. “Award” means an award of Nonqualified Stock Options, Incentive Stock Options, Stock Appreciation Rights, Restricted Shares, Restricted Share Units, or Other Share-Based Awards granted pursuant to the terms and conditions of the Plan. “Award Agreement” means either: (a) an agreement, in written or electronic format, entered into by the Company and a Participant setting forth the terms and provisions applicable to an Award granted under the Plan; or (b) a statement, in written or electronic format, issued by the Company to a Participant describing the terms and provisions of such Award, which need not be signed by the Participant. “Board” means the Board of Directors of the Company. “Cause” shall have the meaning provided in the applicable employment agreement or consulting agreement between, or severance plan covering, the Participant and the Company or a Subsidiary, if any, or if there is no such agreement or plan, as applicable, that defines the term, “Cause” shall mean: (a) the Participant’s repeated failure to satisfactorily perform the Participant’s job duties after thirty (30) days written notice of such deficiency and an opportunity to cure (of at least fifteen business days), as reasonably determined by the Company or a Subsidiary; (b) the Participant’s commission of any act of fraud, misappropriation or embezzlement against or in connection with the Company or any of its Subsidiaries or their respective businesses or operations; (c) the Participant’s commission of, or indictment for or otherwise being formally charged with, any crime involving dishonesty or for any felony; or (d) the engaging by the Participant in misconduct that is detrimental to the financial condition or 13 business reputation of the Company or any of its Subsidiaries, including due to any adverse publicity. “Change in Control” means the occurrence of one of the following events: (a) any “person” (as such term is used in Sections 13(d) and 14(d) of the Exchange Act) becomes the “beneficial owner” (as defined in Rule 13d-3 of the Exchange Act), directly or indirectly, of securities of the Company representing more than fifty percent (50%) of the total voting power represented by the Company’s then-outstanding voting securities; or (b) the consummation of the sale or disposition by the Company of all or substantially all of the Company’s assets; or (c) the consummation of a merger or consolidation of the Company with or into any other entity, other than a merger or consolidation which would result in the voting securities of the Company outstanding immediately prior thereto continuing to represent (either by remaining outstanding or by being converted into voting securities of the surviving entity or its parent) more than fifty percent (50%) of the total voting power represented by the voting securities of the Company or such surviving entity or its parent outstanding immediately after such merger or consolidation. A transaction shall not constitute a Change in Control if its sole purpose is to change the state of the Company’s incorporation or to create a holding company that will be owned in substantially the same proportions by the persons who held the Company’s securities immediately before such transaction. “Code” means the Internal Revenue Code of 1986, as amended. “Committee” means a committee of the Board, as described in Section 3(b). “Company” has the meaning given such term in Section 1(a) and any successor thereto. “Consultant” means a person, excluding Employees and Directors, who performs bona fide services for the Company or a Subsidiary as a consultant or advisor and who qualifies as a consultant or advisor under Rule 701(c)(1) of the Securities Act or under Instruction A.1.(a)(1) of Form S-8 under the Securities Act. “Date of Grant” means the date as of which an Award is determined to be effective and designated in a resolution by the Board and is granted pursuant to the Plan. The Date of Grant shall not be earlier than the date of the resolution and action therein by the Board. “Director” means any individual who is a member of the Board who is not an Employee. “Employee” means any employee of the Company or a Subsidiary, provided that for purposes of determining whether any person may be a Participant for purposes of any grant of an Incentive Stock Option, the term “Employee” has the meaning given to such term in Section 3401(c) of the Code, as interpreted by the regulations thereunder and Applicable Law. “Exchange Act” means the Securities Exchange Act of 1934, as amended, and the rules and regulations thereunder. 14 “Fair Market Value” means, as of any date: (a) if the Shares are not listed or admitted to unlisted trading privileges on a nationally recognized stock exchange, (i) for the purpose of determining the exercise price of, or the amount payable upon the exercise of, Stock Options, Stock Appreciation Rights and any other Award of stock rights that is subject to Section 409A of the Code, the value as determined by the Board through the reasonable application of a reasonable valuation method, taking into account all information material to the value of the Company, within the meaning of Section 409A of the Code, and (ii) for any other purpose, the fair market value as determined by the Board in good faith; or (b) if the Shares are listed on a nationally recognized stock exchange, the closing price of the Shares as reported on the principal nationally recognized stock exchange on which the Shares are traded on such date, or if no Share prices are reported on such date, the closing price of the Shares on the next preceding date on which there were reported Share prices. “Incentive Stock Option” means a Stock Option that is designated as an Incentive Stock Option and that is intended to meet the requirements of Section 422 of the Code. “Nonqualified Stock Option” means a Stock Option that is not intended to meet the requirements of Section 422 of the Code or otherwise does not meet such requirements. “Other Share-Based Award” means an equity-based or equity-related Award not otherwise described by the terms of the Plan, granted in accordance with the terms and conditions set forth in Section 8. “Participant” means any eligible individual as set forth in Section 4 who holds one or more outstanding Awards. “Performance Objectives” means the performance objective or objectives established by the Board pursuant to the Plan. The Performance Objectives applicable to an Award may include, but shall not be limited to, one or more of the following: net earnings or losses (either before or after one or more of interest, taxes, depreciation, amortization, and non-cash equity-based compensation expense); gross or net sales or revenue or sales or revenue growth; net income (either before or after taxes) or adjusted net income; profits (including but not limited to gross profits, net profits, profit growth, net operation profit or economic profit), profit return ratios or operating margin; budget or operating earnings (either before or after taxes or before or after allocation of corporate overhead and bonus); cash flow (including operating cash flow and free cash flow or cash flow return on capital); return on assets; return on capital or invested capital; cost of capital; return on stockholders’ equity; total stockholder return; return on sales; costs, reductions in costs and cost control measures; expenses; working capital; earnings or loss per share; adjusted earnings or loss per share; price per share or dividends per share (or appreciation in or maintenance of such price or dividends); regulatory achievements or compliance; implementation, completion or attainment of objectives relating to research, development, regulatory, commercial, or strategic milestones or developments; market share; economic value or economic valued added models; division, group or corporate financial goals; attainment of strategic and operational initiatives; customer satisfaction/growth; customer service; employee satisfaction; recruitment and maintenance of personnel; human resources management; supervision of litigation and other legal matters; strategic partnerships and 15 transactions; financial ratios (including those measuring liquidity, activity, profitability or leverage); debt levels or reductions; sales-related goals; financing and other capital raising transactions; year-end cash; acquisition activity; investment sourcing activity; and marketing initiatives, any of which may be measured in absolute terms or as compared to any incremental increase or decrease, peer group results, or market performance indicators or indices. “Plan” has the meaning given such term in Section 1(a). “Restatement Date” has the meaning given such term in Section 1(a). “Restricted Shares” means Shares granted or sold pursuant to Section 6 as to which neither the substantial risk of forfeiture nor the prohibition on transfers referred to in such Section 6 has expired. “Restricted Share Unit” means a grant or sale of the right to receive Shares or cash at the end of a specified restriction period made pursuant to Section 7. “Securities Act” means the Securities Act of 1933, as amended, and the rules and regulations thereunder. “Share” means a share of common stock of the Company, $0.001 par value per share, or any security into which such Share may be changed by reason of any transaction or event of the type referred to in Section 10. “Stock Appreciation Right” means a right designated as such and granted pursuant to Section 5. “Stock Option” means a right to purchase a Share granted to a Participant under the Plan in accordance with the terms and conditions set forth in Section 5. Stock Options may be either Incentive Stock Options or Nonqualified Stock Options. “Subsidiary” means: (a) with respect to an Incentive Stock Option, a “subsidiary corporation” as defined under Section 424(f) of the Code; and (b) for all other purposes under the Plan, any corporation or other entity in which the Company owns, directly or indirectly, a proprietary interest of more than fifty percent by reason of stock ownership or otherwise. “Ten Percent Stockholder” means any Participant who owns more than ten percent of the combined voting power of all classes of stock of the Company, within the meaning of Section 422 of the Code. [END OF DOCUMENT] 16

title: GP-Act III Acquisition Corp.
text: EX-10.1 3 ea031085801ex10-1.htm SPONSOR LETTER AGREEMENT, DATED AS OF NOVEMBER 3, 2026, BY AND AMONG GP-ACT III SPONSOR LLC, THE INSIDERS NAMED THEREIN, GP-ACT III ACQUISITION CORP. AND DRONAMICS GROUP LIMITED Exhibit 10.1 CONFIDENTIAL Execution Version SPONSOR LETTER AGREEMENT This Sponsor Letter Agreement (this “ Agreement ”) is dated as of November 3, 2026, by and among GP-Act III Sponsor LLC, a Cayman Islands limited liability company (the “ Sponsor ”), each of the other Persons listed on the signature pages hereto as an “Insider” (each, an “ Insider ” and, together with the Sponsor, the “ Sponsor Parties ”), GP-Act III Acquisition Corp., a Cayman Islands exempted company limited by shares (which will domesticate as a Delaware corporation prior to the Closing) (“ Holdco ”), a Delaware corporation to be incorporated prior to the Closing and to become a party hereto pursuant to a joinder agreement (“ Newco ”), and Dronamics Group Limited, a private company limited by shares incorporated and registered in Ireland (the “ Company ”). Capitalized terms used but not defined herein have the meanings given to them in the Business Combination Agreement (as defined below). RECITALS WHEREAS, as of the date hereof, the Sponsor Parties are the holders of record of the Holdco Securities set forth opposite their names on Schedule I hereto, including an aggregate of 7,187,500 Founder Shares and 4,500,000 Holdco Warrants (such securities, together with any New Securities (as defined below), the “ Subject Securities ”); WHEREAS, the Sponsor is managed and controlled exclusively by its managing members, GPIAC II, LLC, IDS III LLC and Boxcar Partners III, LLC (collectively, the “ Co-Sponsors ”), and certain non-managing members of the Sponsor (the “ Non-Managing Investors ”) hold membership interests in the Sponsor reflecting indirect interests in 3,220,000 Founder Shares and 4,025,000 of the Holdco Warrants held by the Sponsor, which securities, as provided herein, shall not be subject to the forfeiture and earnout provisions of Article II ; WHEREAS, pursuant to certain non-redemption agreements entered into on or about May 11, 2026 by Holdco and the Sponsor with certain shareholders of Holdco (the “ Existing Non-Redemption Agreements ”), the Sponsor has agreed to transfer an aggregate of 403,720 Founder Shares to such shareholders in connection with or promptly following the Closing, and such Founder Shares shall likewise not be subject to the forfeiture and earnout provisions of Article II ; WHEREAS, contemporaneously with the execution and delivery of this Agreement, Holdco and the Company are entering into a Business Combination Agreement, dated as of the date hereof (as amended, restated, supplemented or otherwise modified from time to time in accordance with its terms, the “ Business Combination Agreement ”), pursuant to which, subject to the terms and conditions therein, among other things, (a) Holdco will effect the Holdco Domestication, (b) the Company will effect the Company Reorganization, as a result of which the Company will become a wholly-owned subsidiary of Newco, and (c) a Delaware corporation and a wholly-owned subsidiary of Holdco will merge with and into Newco pursuant to the Merger, with Newco surviving as a wholly-owned subsidiary of Holdco and each share of Newco Stock being converted into the right to receive a portion of the Merger Consideration (the Holdco Domestication, the Company Reorganization and the Merger, together with the other transactions contemplated by the Business Combination Agreement and the Ancillary Documents, the “ Transactions ”); and WHEREAS, as a condition and inducement to the willingness of Holdco, Newco and the Company to enter into the Business Combination Agreement and to consummate the transactions contemplated thereby, the parties hereto desire to agree to certain matters as set forth herein. NOW, THEREFORE, in consideration of the foregoing and the mutual covenants and agreements contained herein, and for other good and valuable consideration, the receipt and sufficiency of which are hereby acknowledged, the parties hereto, intending to be legally bound hereby, agree as follows: Article I SUPPORT AND COVENANTS Section 1.1 Voting . Following the date hereof and prior to the Expiration Time (as defined below), at any meeting of the Holdco Shareholders (including the Extension Shareholders’ Meeting and the Holdco Shareholders’ Meeting), whether annual or special, however called, and at any adjournment or postponement thereof, and in connection with any action by written consent or resolution of the Holdco Shareholders with respect to which any Sponsor Party is entitled to vote or consent, each Sponsor Party shall (a) appear or otherwise cause all of its Subject Securities entitled to vote to be counted as present thereat for purposes of establishing a quorum and (b) vote (in person or by proxy), or cause to be voted (or consent to any action by written consent with respect to), all of its respective Subject Securities entitled to vote: (i) in favor of the Holdco Extension Approval and each Transaction Proposal; (ii) against any Business Combination Proposal or Holdco Acquisition Proposal (other than the Transactions) and any proposal relating thereto; (iii) against any other merger, consolidation, combination, sale of substantial assets, reorganization, recapitalization, dissolution, liquidation or winding up of or by Holdco (other than pursuant to the Business Combination Agreement and the Ancillary Documents); (iv) against any change in the business, management or board of directors of Holdco (other than as contemplated by the Transaction Proposals or pursuant to the Business Combination Agreement and the Ancillary Documents); and (v) against any other proposal, action or agreement involving Holdco that would reasonably be expected to (A) prevent, materially impede or delay or otherwise adversely affect in any material respect the Transactions, (B) result in a breach of any covenant, representation, warranty or other obligation of Holdco under the Business Combination Agreement or of any Sponsor Party under this Agreement or any Ancillary Document or (C) result in any condition set forth in Article IX of the Business Combination Agreement not being satisfied. No Sponsor Party shall commit or agree to take any action set forth in this Section 1.1 inconsistent with the foregoing. 2 The obligations of the Sponsor Parties under this Section 1.1 shall apply whether or not the Transactions are recommended by the board of directors of Holdco, and whether or not any previous such recommendation has been withdrawn, modified, qualified or otherwise changed by such board of directors. Section 1.2 No Shop . Prior to the Expiration Time, each of the Sponsor Parties, severally and not jointly, agrees not to, and shall cause its controlled Affiliates not to, and shall direct its and their respective directors, officers, employees, agents and representatives acting on its or their behalf (collectively, “ Sponsor Representatives ”) not to, directly or indirectly, (i) make any proposal or offer that constitutes a Business Combination Proposal, (ii) initiate any discussions or negotiations with any Person with respect to a Business Combination Proposal or (iii) enter into any acquisition agreement, business combination, merger agreement or similar definitive agreement, or any letter of intent, memorandum of understanding or agreement in principle, or any other agreement relating to a Business Combination Proposal; provided , however , that nothing in this Section 1.2 shall prohibit any Sponsor Party, its controlled Affiliates or its or their Sponsor Representatives from engaging in discussions or negotiations regarding, or entering into an agreement in respect of, a Holdco Acquisition Proposal, so long as (w) such Holdco Acquisition Proposal does not constitute a Business Combination Proposal, (x) the consummation thereof is conditioned upon, and occurs only following, the Effective Time, and (y) such Holdco Acquisition Proposal would not reasonably be expected to prevent, impair, impede or delay the consummation of the Merger or the performance by Holdco of its obligations under the Business Combination Agreement or by such Sponsor Party of its obligations hereunder, or impose any obligation or liability on the Company, Newco or any of their respective Subsidiaries. From and after the date hereof, each Sponsor Party shall, and shall cause its controlled Affiliates to, and shall direct its and their Sponsor Representatives to, immediately cease and terminate all discussions and negotiations with any Persons that may be ongoing with respect to a Business Combination Proposal. For the avoidance of doubt, (A) no Non-Managing Investor or other direct or indirect equityholder, limited partner or member of the Sponsor or any Co-Sponsor (in each case, not acting on behalf of a Sponsor Party) shall be bound by, or be deemed a Sponsor Representative for purposes of, this Section 1.2 , and (B) nothing in this Section 1.2 shall restrict any other special purpose acquisition company, investment fund, vehicle or portfolio company sponsored, managed or advised by any Co-Sponsor or any of its Affiliates from evaluating, negotiating or consummating any transaction that does not involve Holdco or its securities. Section 1.3 Waiver of Redemption Rights . Each Sponsor Party irrevocably agrees that if Holdco seeks shareholder approval of (i) the Transactions or (ii) the Holdco Extension Approval, including, in each case, any amendments to the Holdco Governing Documents, such Sponsor Party shall not elect to redeem, or tender or submit for redemption, any of its Subject Securities in connection with such shareholder approval, and shall comply with its obligations under the letter agreement, dated May 8, 2024, among Holdco, the Sponsor and the other parties thereto (the “ Insider Letter ”). Neither the Sponsor nor Holdco shall amend or terminate or waive any provision of the Insider Letter in a manner that would reasonably be expected to prevent, impede or delay the Transactions without the prior written consent of the Company. Section 1.4 No Transfer . Except as expressly contemplated by the Business Combination Agreement or this Agreement, during the period from the date hereof until the earliest of (a) the Closing, (b) the valid termination of the Business Combination Agreement in accordance with its terms and (c) the liquidation of Holdco (the “ Expiration Time ”), no Sponsor Party shall, without the prior written consent of the Company, directly or indirectly (i) sell, offer to sell, contract or agree to sell, assign, pledge, hypothecate, grant any option to purchase or otherwise dispose of any Subject Securities, (ii) enter into any swap, hedge or other arrangement that transfers to another, in whole or in part, any of the economic consequences of ownership of any Subject Securities or (iii) publicly announce any intention to effect any of the foregoing (i) or (ii) (each, a “ Transfer ”), other than a Permitted Transfer. “ Permitted Transfer ” means a Transfer (A) to any officer or director of Holdco or the Sponsor, any Affiliate thereof or any immediate family member of such officer or director, (B) to any Co-Sponsor, any direct or indirect member, partner or equity holder of the Sponsor or any Co-Sponsor, or any investment fund or vehicle controlled or managed by the Sponsor, any Co-Sponsor or any of their respective Affiliates, (C) in the case of an individual, by gift to a member of such individual’s immediate family or to a trust the beneficiaries of which are such individual or members of such individual’s immediate family, to a charitable organization, by virtue of the laws of descent and distribution upon the death of such individual or pursuant to a qualified domestic relations order, (D) by operation of law or court order, (E) pursuant to the Existing Non-Redemption Agreements or any Additional Investor Arrangement, in each case as contemplated by Section 2.5 , or (F) as otherwise agreed in writing by Holdco and the Company; provided that, in the case of clauses (A) through (D) and (F), the transferee agrees in writing to be bound by this Agreement with respect to the transferred Subject Securities, and no Permitted Transfer shall relieve the transferring Sponsor Party of its obligations hereunder. 3 Section 1.5 New Securities . Any Holdco Securities issued to, or acquired (including by purchase, conversion, stock dividend, split, recapitalization or otherwise) by, any Sponsor Party after the date hereof, or with respect to which any Sponsor Party acquires the right to vote after the date hereof and prior to the Expiration Time (the “ New Securities ”), shall be subject to this Agreement as if they were Subject Securities held on the date hereof. References in this Agreement to the Founder Shares, the Holdco Warrants, the Sponsor Private Placement Warrants and the Subject Securities shall be deemed to refer to and include (a) the Domesticated Holdco Common Shares and Domesticated Holdco Warrants into which such securities are converted pursuant to the Holdco Conversion, (b) the Holdco Common Shares and warrants to purchase Holdco Common Shares held following the Merger, and (c) any securities into which or for which any of the foregoing may be changed or exchanged by reason of any share dividend or distribution, split, reverse split, consolidation, recapitalization, combination, conversion, exchange or similar transaction. Section 1.6 Waiver of Anti-Dilution Rights . Subject to, and conditioned upon, the consummation of the Transactions, each Sponsor Party irrevocably waives, to the fullest extent permitted by applicable Law and the Holdco Governing Documents, and covenants and agrees not to exercise, assert or perfect, any right to adjustment of any anti-dilution or similar protection with respect to any Founder Shares arising from the Transactions. Section 1.7 No Challenges . No Sponsor Party shall commence, join or participate (and each shall take all actions necessary to opt out of any class in any class action with respect to) any Action, derivative or otherwise, against Holdco, the Company or any of their respective Affiliates or any of the foregoing Persons’ respective successors or assigns (a) challenging the validity of, or seeking to enjoin the operation of, any provision of this Agreement or the Business Combination Agreement, or (b) alleging a breach of fiduciary duty of any Person in connection with the evaluation, negotiation, entry into or performance of this Agreement, the Business Combination Agreement and the Ancillary Documents, or consummation of the Transactions; provided that nothing herein shall restrict any Sponsor Party from enforcing its rights under this Agreement, the Business Combination Agreement (solely to the extent such Sponsor Party is an express third-party beneficiary thereof or is otherwise expressly granted rights thereunder), the Insider Letter or any Ancillary Document to which it is a party. 4 Section 1.8 Closing Deliverables . At the Closing, the Sponsor Parties shall deliver to Holdco duly executed counterparts of the Amended and Restated Registration Rights Agreement, in a form to be mutually agreed by the parties thereto prior to the Closing. Section 1.9 Further Assurances . Each party hereto shall take, or cause to be taken, all actions and do, or cause to be done, all things reasonably necessary under applicable Law to consummate the Transactions on the terms and subject to the conditions set forth herein and in the Business Combination Agreement, including the execution and delivery of any further documents, agreements or instruments of assignment, transfer or conveyance as may be reasonably necessary to effectuate the purposes hereof and thereof and as may be reasonably requested in writing by another party hereto. The Company shall cause Newco, promptly (and in any event within five (5) Business Days) following its incorporation and in any event prior to the commencement of the Company Reorganization, to execute and deliver to the other parties hereto a joinder agreement, in form and substance reasonably satisfactory to Holdco and the Sponsor, pursuant to which Newco shall become a party to this Agreement with the same force and effect as if it were an original signatory hereto. Section 1.10 No Inconsistent Voting Arrangements; No Proxy Solicitation. Prior to the Expiration Time, no Sponsor Party shall, and each Sponsor Party shall cause its Affiliates not to, (a) deposit any Subject Securities in a voting trust or subject any Subject Securities to any proxy, arrangement or agreement with respect to the voting thereof, other than as contemplated by this Agreement or as requested in writing by Holdco and the Company in connection with the Transactions, or (b) except as contemplated by the Business Combination Agreement in furtherance of the Transactions, make, or in any manner participate in, directly or indirectly, a “solicitation” of “proxies” or consents (as such terms are used in the rules of the SEC) with respect to the voting of any Holdco Securities in opposition to the Transactions; provided that recommending that the Holdco Shareholders vote in favor of the Transaction Proposals shall not constitute such a solicitation. Section 1.11 Information; Disclosure . Prior to the Expiration Time, each Sponsor Party shall provide to Holdco, Newco and the Company any information regarding such Sponsor Party or its Subject Securities that is reasonably requested in connection with the Registration Statement, the Joint Proxy Statement or any other Offer Document. Each Sponsor Party authorizes Holdco, Newco and the Company to publish and disclose, to the extent required by applicable Law, the SEC or NASDAQ, such Sponsor Party’s identity and ownership of Subject Securities and the nature of its commitments under this Agreement; provided that such disclosure is made in compliance with the Business Combination Agreement and the terms hereof. 5 Article II FOUNDER SHARES AND SPONSOR WARRANTS Section 2.1 Certain Definitions . For purposes of this Article II : (a) “ Adjusted NCDC ” means (A) the Closing Date Cash minus (B) the Holdco Transaction Expenses, in each case expressed in U.S. dollars, as set forth in the Holdco Financing Certificate and the Forfeiture Schedule; provided that, for purposes of this Agreement only, Adjusted NCDC shall include, to the extent not otherwise included in the Closing Date Cash, (i) the aggregate gross cash proceeds actually funded to the Company under the Convertible Notes prior to the Closing and (ii) the aggregate gross cash proceeds of any other financing funded by the Co-Sponsors or their Affiliates to Holdco or the Company concurrently with or following the execution of the Business Combination Agreement; provided further that, solely for purposes of calculating the percentages under Section 2.2 , Adjusted NCDC shall be deemed to be zero if negative; (b) “ Excluded Founder Shares ” means (i) the 75,000 Founder Shares held of record by the Insiders, (ii) the 3,220,000 Founder Shares attributable to the membership interests of the Non-Managing Investors in the Sponsor, (iii) the 403,720 Founder Shares that the Sponsor is obligated to transfer pursuant to the Existing Non-Redemption Agreements and (iv) any Founder Shares that the Sponsor is obligated to transfer pursuant to any Additional Investor Arrangement; (c) “ Forfeitable Founder Shares ” means all Founder Shares held by the Sponsor Parties as of immediately prior to the Forfeiture Time, other than the Excluded Founder Shares, being, as of the date hereof and before giving effect to any Additional Investor Arrangement, 3,488,780 Founder Shares; (d) “ Sponsor Private Placement Warrants ” means the 4,500,000 Holdco Warrants issued to the Sponsor as “Private Placement Warrants” under the Warrant Agreement; (e) “ Excluded Sponsor Warrants ” means (i) the 4,025,000 Sponsor Private Placement Warrants attributable to the membership interests of the Non-Managing Investors in the Sponsor and (ii) any Sponsor Private Placement Warrants that the Sponsor is obligated to transfer pursuant to any Additional Investor Arrangement; (f) “ Forfeitable Sponsor Warrants ” means the Sponsor Private Placement Warrants held by the Sponsor as of immediately prior to the Forfeiture Time, other than the Excluded Sponsor Warrants, being, as of the date hereof, 475,000 Sponsor Private Placement Warrants; (g) “ Forfeiture Time ” means the time on the Closing Date immediately following the Holdco Conversion and immediately prior to the Effective Time; (h) “ Warrant Agreement ” means the Warrant Agreement, dated May 8, 2024, between Holdco and Continental Stock Transfer & Trust Company, as warrant agent; (i) “ Retained Percentage ”, “ Earnout Percentage ” and “ Forfeited Percentage ” have the meanings given in Section 2.2 , as applicable; (j) “ Earnout Founder Shares ” means the Forfeitable Founder Shares corresponding to the Earnout Percentage that become subject to vesting pursuant to Sections 2.2 and 2.3 ; (k) “ Earnout Period ” means the period commencing on the Closing Date and ending on the fifth (5th) anniversary of the Closing Date; (l) “ Vesting Event ” means the first date during the Earnout Period on which the volume-weighted average price of one Holdco Common Share on NASDAQ (or such other national securities exchange on which the Holdco Common Shares are then listed), calculated as the arithmetic average of the daily volume-weighted average prices as reported by Bloomberg L.P. for each Trading Day in such period, over any period of ninety (90) consecutive Trading Days exceeds $14.00 (as equitably adjusted for any stock split, reverse stock split, stock dividend, reorganization, recapitalization, reclassification, combination or exchange of shares after the Closing); and (m) “ Trading Day ” means any day on which NASDAQ (or such other exchange) is open for trading. 6 Section 2.2 Retention, Forfeiture and Earnout of Founder Shares . Effective as of the Forfeiture Time, and conditioned upon the occurrence of the Closing, the Forfeitable Founder Shares shall be treated as follows (each percentage below being a percentage of the Forfeitable Founder Shares ). The Excluded Founder Shares shall not be subject to this Section 2.2 or to Section 2.3 . (a) If Adjusted NCDC is less than or equal to $25,000,000: (i) the Retained Percentage shall be twenty-five percent (25%); (ii) the Earnout Percentage shall be equal to twenty-five percent (25%) multiplied by the quotient of Adjusted NCDC divided by $25,000,000; and (iii) the Forfeited Percentage shall be equal to one hundred percent (100%) minus the sum of (x) the Retained Percentage, and (y) the Earnout Percentage. (b) If Adjusted NCDC is greater than $25,000,000 but less than $100,000,000: with “X” meaning the quotient of (A) Adjusted NCDC minus $25,000,000, divided by (B) $75,000,000, (i) the Retained Percentage shall be equal to 25% + (75% × X); (ii) the Earnout Percentage shall be equal to 25% × (1 − X); and (iii) the Forfeited Percentage shall be equal to one hundred percent (100%) minus the sum of (x) the Retained Percentage, and (y) the Earnout Percentage. (c) If Adjusted NCDC is equal to or greater than $100,000,000: the Retained Percentage shall be one hundred percent (100%) and the Earnout Percentage and the Forfeited Percentage shall each be zero. (d) The Forfeitable Founder Shares corresponding to the Forfeited Percentage (the “ Forfeited Founder Shares ”) shall, at the Forfeiture Time, be surrendered by the Sponsor to Holdco for no consideration and cancelled, and no Sponsor Party shall have any further right in respect thereof. The Forfeitable Founder Shares corresponding to the Retained Percentage (the “ Retained Founder Shares ”) shall remain outstanding and shall not be subject to any forfeiture, vesting or earnout condition (but shall be subject to the lock-up set forth in the Amended and Restated Registration Rights Agreement, as applicable). The Forfeitable Founder Shares corresponding to the Earnout Percentage shall remain issued and outstanding following the Closing as Earnout Founder Shares subject to Section 2.3 . The allocation of the Retained Founder Shares, Earnout Founder Shares and Forfeited Founder Shares among the Co-Sponsors shall be determined in accordance with the organizational documents of the Sponsor and shall not affect the Excluded Founder Shares. All fractional shares shall be rounded down to the nearest whole share, and any remaining Forfeitable Founder Shares resulting from such rounding shall be included in the Retained Founder Shares. Illustrative outcomes are set forth on Annex A . Section 2.3 Vesting of Earnout Founder Shares . The Earnout Founder Shares shall vest automatically in full (without further action by any Person) upon the occurrence of the Vesting Event. Prior to vesting, the Earnout Founder Shares (a) may not be Transferred (other than pursuant to a Permitted Transfer to a transferee that agrees in writing to be bound by this Section 2.3 ), (b) shall be counted as present for purposes of determining a quorum at any meeting of the stockholders of Holdco and, at any such meeting and in any action by written consent of the stockholders of Holdco, shall be voted (or consents shall be given or withheld) by the holder thereof for, against and abstaining with respect to each matter in the same proportion as the Holdco Common Shares (other than Earnout Founder Shares) that are voted for or against, or abstain with respect to, such matter (it being understood that shares that are not present, broker non-votes and shares not otherwise voted shall be disregarded for purposes of such calculation, and that if no such other Holdco Common Shares are so voted, the Earnout Founder Shares shall be deemed not voted on such matter), and the Sponsor shall take all actions reasonably necessary to give effect to the foregoing; provided that this clause (b) shall cease to apply to any Earnout Founder Share upon its vesting in accordance with Section 2.2 , and (c) shall not be entitled to receive dividends or other distributions (which shall be held by Holdco and paid upon, and only upon, vesting). Any Earnout Founder Shares that have not vested on or before the last day of the Earnout Period shall be automatically surrendered to Holdco and cancelled for no consideration on such day. If, during the Earnout Period, Holdco consummates a merger, consolidation, business combination, sale of all or substantially all of its assets or other similar transaction in which the holders of Holdco Common Shares receive or are entitled to receive consideration having an aggregate value of at least $14.00 per share, the Earnout Founder Shares shall vest immediately prior to such transaction. Holdco shall cause its transfer agent to reflect the restrictions in this Section 2.3 by book-entry notation and to remove such restrictions promptly upon vesting of the applicable Earnout Founder Shares. 7 Section 2.4 Sponsor Warrants . Effective as of the Forfeiture Time, and conditioned upon the occurrence of the Closing, the Retained Percentage, the Earnout Percentage and the Forfeited Percentage shall be applied to the Forfeitable Sponsor Warrants. The Excluded Sponsor Warrants shall not be subject to this Section 2.4 . Accordingly, (a) the Forfeitable Sponsor Warrants corresponding to the Retained Percentage shall remain outstanding and exercisable in accordance with their terms and the Warrant Agreement, (b) the Sponsor shall not exercise, and shall not Transfer (other than pursuant to a Permitted Transfer to a transferee that agrees in writing to be bound by this Section 2.4 ), the Forfeitable Sponsor Warrants corresponding to the Earnout Percentage (the “ Earnout Sponsor Warrants ”) unless and until the Vesting Event occurs during the Earnout Period, whereupon such restrictions shall lapse, and (c) the Forfeitable Sponsor Warrants corresponding to the Forfeited Percentage shall be surrendered by the Sponsor to Holdco for no consideration and cancelled at the Forfeiture Time. Any Earnout Sponsor Warrants with respect to which the Vesting Event has not occurred by the end of the Earnout Period shall be surrendered to Holdco and cancelled for no consideration. Holdco shall cause the warrant agent under the Warrant Agreement to reflect the restrictions in this Section 2.4 by book-entry notation and to remove such restrictions promptly upon the Vesting Event. All fractional warrants shall be rounded down to the nearest whole warrant, and any remaining Forfeitable Sponsor Warrants resulting from such rounding shall be included in the Forfeitable Sponsor Warrants corresponding to the Retained Percentage. Section 2.5 Excluded Securities; Investor Arrangements . The Sponsor may, prior to the Closing, enter into additional non-redemption agreements or similar arrangements with Holdco Shareholders in connection with any extension of Holdco’s Business Combination deadline, the Holdco Shareholder Approval or the Transactions, or agree to transfer Founder Shares or Sponsor Private Placement Warrants to PIPE Investors or other investors in connection with any Subscription Agreement or other financing in connection with the Transactions (each, an “ Additional Investor Arrangement ”), in each case as permitted by Section 7.10 and Section 8.6 of the Business Combination Agreement; provided that the Sponsor shall give the Company written notice of each Additional Investor Arrangement, including the number of Founder Shares and Sponsor Private Placement Warrants to be transferred thereunder, promptly (and in any event within five (5) Business Days) after entering into it and in any event prior to the delivery of the Holdco Financing Certificate. Any Founder Shares or Sponsor Private Placement Warrants transferred or to be transferred pursuant to the Existing Non-Redemption Agreements or any Additional Investor Arrangement (a) shall constitute Excluded Founder Shares or Excluded Sponsor Warrants, as applicable, (b) shall not be subject to Section 2.2 , Section 2.3 or Section 2.4 and (c) shall be subject only to such lock-up (if any) as is provided in the applicable agreement with the applicable transferee. Any such incentive or consideration shall be borne solely by the Sponsor and shall not reduce Closing Date Cash or Net Closing Date Cash. For the avoidance of doubt, nothing in this Section 2.5 shall require the Sponsor to enter into any financing arrangement or undertake any transfer obligation beyond those expressly agreed to by the Sponsor. 8 Section 2.6 Determination; Forfeiture Mechanics; Warrant Consents . (a) Holdco shall deliver to the Sponsor and the Company, together with the Holdco Financing Certificate, a schedule setting forth in reasonable detail the calculation of the Adjusted NCDC, the Retained Percentage, the Earnout Percentage and the Forfeited Percentage and the resulting number of Retained Founder Shares, Earnout Founder Shares and Forfeited Founder Shares and of Forfeitable Sponsor Warrants in each category (the “ Forfeiture Schedule ”). Absent manifest error, the Forfeiture Schedule shall be final and binding on the parties for purposes of this Agreement, and no post-Closing adjustment, reconciliation or true-up shall be made to the Adjusted NCDC or the Forfeiture Schedule. (b) At or prior to the Forfeiture Time, the Sponsor shall deliver to Holdco such stock powers, instructions to Holdco’s transfer agent and to the warrant agent under the Warrant Agreement and other instruments as are reasonably necessary to effect the surrender and cancellation contemplated by this Article II , and each of Holdco and the Sponsor shall take all corporate and other actions reasonably necessary to give effect thereto. Section 2.7 Post-Closing Covenants of Holdco . From and after the Closing, Holdco shall (a) promptly (and in any event within five (5) Business Days) after the occurrence of the Vesting Event, deliver to the Sponsor written confirmation thereof, (b) cause the restrictive notations in respect of the Earnout Founder Shares and the Earnout Sponsor Warrants to be removed promptly following the Vesting Event and (c) pay to the holders of Earnout Founder Shares, promptly upon vesting, all dividends and other distributions withheld in respect thereof pursuant to Section 2.3 . The Sponsor shall be entitled to enforce this Section 2.7 directly against Holdco. Article III REPRESENTATIONS AND WARRANTIES Section 3.1 Representations and Warranties . (a) Each party hereto represents and warrants that: If an entity, it is duly organized, validly existing and in good standing under the Laws of its jurisdiction of organization, and the execution, delivery and performance of this Agreement are within its powers and have been duly and validly authorized by all corporate or limited liability company action on its part. It has the power and authority, or capacity, as the case may be, to enter into this Agreement and to carry out its obligations hereunder. This Agreement has been duly executed and delivered by it and constitutes its legal, valid and binding obligation, enforceable in accordance with its terms, subject to applicable bankruptcy, insolvency and similar Laws and general principles of equity. 9 (b) Each Sponsor Party, severally and not jointly, represents and warrants to Holdco and the Company, as of the date hereof, that it is the record owner of, and has good title to, the Subject Securities set forth opposite its name on Schedule I hereto, free and clear of all Liens other than Liens arising under this Agreement, the Holdco Governing Documents, the Business Combination Agreement, the Ancillary Documents, the Insider Letter, its organizational documents or applicable securities Laws. Such Subject Securities are the only Holdco Securities owned of record by it, and are not subject to any proxy, voting trust or other voting arrangement except as provided hereunder, the governing documents of the Sponsor and under the Insider Letter. (c) Except for the representations and warranties expressly set forth in this Section 3.1 , no party hereto nor any other Person makes any express or implied representation or warranty in connection with this Agreement or the Transactions, and each party expressly disclaims any such other representations or warranties. Article IV MISCELLANEOUS Section 4.1 Termination . This Agreement shall terminate upon the earliest of (a) the valid termination of the Business Combination Agreement in accordance with its terms prior to the Closing, (b) the liquidation of Holdco and (c) the written agreement of the Sponsor, Holdco and the Company. In the event that the Business Combination Agreement is terminated in accordance with its terms prior to the Closing, this Agreement shall be of no force and effect automatically (and without further action by any Person) from and after such termination; provided that no termination shall relieve any party from liability for any fraud or willful breach of this Agreement by such party occurring prior to such termination. Article II and this Article IV shall survive the Closing. Section 4.2 Assignment . This Agreement shall be binding upon and inure to the benefit of the parties and their respective heirs, successors and permitted assigns. No party hereto may, except as set forth herein, assign this Agreement or any of its rights or obligations hereunder without the prior written consent of the other parties. Any purported assignment in violation of this Section shall be void and ineffectual and shall not operate to transfer or assign any right, interest or obligation to the purported assignee. Section 4.3 Amendment . This Agreement may not be amended, supplemented or otherwise modified except by a written instrument (i) prior to the Closing, executed by the Sponsor, Holdco, Newco (following its joinder hereto) and the Company, it being agreed that the execution of any such instrument by the Company and Newco shall not be required after any termination of the Business Combination Agreement in accordance with its terms, and (ii) after the Closing, executed by the Sponsor and Holdco. Any provision of this Agreement may be waived only by a written instrument executed by the party against whom such waiver is to be effective. Section 4.4 Incorporation by Reference . Sections 1.2 ( Construction ), 11.1 ( Trust Account Waiver ), 11.2 ( Waiver ), 11.3 ( Notices ), 11.5 ( Rights of Third Parties ), 11.7 ( Governing Law ), 11.8 ( Captions; Counterparts ), 11.10 ( Entire Agreement ), 11.13 ( Severability ), 11.14 ( Jurisdiction; Waiver of Jury Trial ) and 11.15 ( Enforcement ) of the Business Combination Agreement shall apply mutatis mutandis to this Agreement. Subject to the foregoing, all notices and other communications to a Sponsor Party shall be sent to the address set forth on Schedule I . 10 Section 4.5 Capacity . Notwithstanding anything in this Agreement to the contrary, (a) each Sponsor Party makes no agreement or understanding herein in any capacity other than in its capacity as a record holder of Subject Securities, and not in its (or any of its representatives’) capacity as a director, officer or employee of Holdco or any of its Subsidiaries, as applicable, and (b) nothing herein shall be construed to limit or affect any action or inaction by any Sponsor Party or any representative of any Sponsor Party serving as a member of the board of directors or as an officer, employee or fiduciary of Holdco or any of its Subsidiaries, as applicable, in each case acting in such Person’s capacity as a director, officer, employee or fiduciary. Section 4.6 No Recourse . This Agreement may only be enforced against, and any claim based upon, arising out of or related to this Agreement may only be brought against, the Persons that are expressly named as parties hereto, and then only with respect to the specific obligations set forth herein with respect to such party. No past, present or future director, officer, employee, incorporator, member, partner, equityholder, Affiliate, agent or representative of any Sponsor Party (other than the Sponsor Parties themselves, in accordance with the terms hereof) shall have any liability for any obligations or liabilities of any party under this Agreement. Section 4.7 Several Obligations . The obligations of the Sponsor Parties under this Agreement are several and not joint, and no Sponsor Party shall be liable for any breach of this Agreement by any other Sponsor Party.
